title.raw: 卷二十一 志第一: 禮儀一 Volume 21 Treatises 1: Rites 1

sentences.zh: 唐禮：四時各以孟月享太廟，每室用太牢，季冬蠟祭之後，以辰日臘享於太廟，用牲如時祭。

translations.literal: Tang rites: In each of the four seasons, in the first month of the season, offerings were made to the Great Ancestral Temple; for each chamber the great offering was used. After the wax sacrifices following the twelfth month's la rites, on a chen day a la offering was presented at the Great Temple, with victims as at the seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ritual: each season's first month, offerings at the Great Temple—tai lao per chamber. After twelfth-month wax and la, a chen-day la feast at the temple used seasonal victims.

sentences.zh: 三年一祫，以孟冬。

translations.literal: Every three years a he sacrifice, in the first month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: A he rite every three years, in mid-winter's opening month.

sentences.zh: 五年一禘，以孟夏。

translations.literal: Every five years a di sacrifice, in the first month of summer.
translations.idiomatic: A di rite every five years, in mid-summer's opening month.

sentences.zh: 又時享之日，修七祀於太廟西門內之道南：司命，戶以春，灶以夏；

translations.literal: On days of seasonal offerings, the Seven Sacrifices were maintained on the road south within the western gate of the Great Temple: Spirit of Fate; the Household Spirit in spring, the Stove Spirit in summer;
translations.idiomatic: On seasonal offering days the Seven Sacrifices were kept on the lane south of the temple's west gate—Spirit of Fate; Household Spirit in spring, Stove Spirit in summer;

sentences.zh: 門，厲以秋，行以冬，中溜則于季夏迎氣日祀之。

translations.literal: the Gate Spirit and the Pestilence Spirit in autumn, the Road Spirit in winter; the Central Gutter was sacrificed on the day of receiving seasonal qi in the last month of summer.
translations.idiomatic: Gate and Pestilence Spirits in autumn, Road Spirit in winter; Central Gutter on the last-summer qi-reception day.

sentences.zh: 若品物時新堪進御者，所司先送太常，與尚食相知，簡擇精好者，以滋味與新物相宜者配之。

translations.literal: If seasonal novelties were fit to present to the sovereign, the responsible office first sent them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and coordinated with the Imperial Provisioners, selecting the finest and pairing them with flavors suited to the new goods.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal delicacies fit for the throne went first to the Court of Sacrifices and the Provisioners, who picked the best and matched flavor to the new offering.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奉薦於太廟，不出神主。

translations.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices presented offerings at the Great Temple without bringing out the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Sacrifices presented at the Great Temple without removing the tablets.

sentences.zh: 仲春薦冰，亦如之。

translations.literal: In mid-spring ice was presented—in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring ice offerings followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 五月，備法駕迎宣簡公，懿王、景皇帝、元皇帝神主，祔於太廟，始享四室。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, with the full imperial escort, the spirit tablets of Duke Xuanjian, King Yi, Emperor Jing, and Emperor Yuan were welcomed and enshrined in the Great Temple, and for the first time four chambers received offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: full escort welcomed tablets of Duke Xuanjian, King Yi, Emperor Jing, and Emperor Yuan into the Great Temple; four chambers were offered to for the first time.

sentences.zh: ，高祖崩，將行遷祔之禮，太宗命有司詳議廟制。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, they were about to perform the relocation-enshrinement rite; Taizong ordered the relevant offices to deliberate in detail on temple regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's death was to trigger relocation-enshrinement; Taizong ordered a full review of temple rules.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫朱子奢建議曰：

translations.literal: Remonstrance Adviser Zhu Zisha memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Adviser Zhu Zisha proposed:

sentences.zh: 於是八座奏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eight Ministers memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers then submitted:

sentences.zh: 制從之。

translations.literal: The decree followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 於是增修太廟，始崇祔弘農府君及高祖神主，並舊四室為六室。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Great Temple was enlarged and renovated; for the first time the spirit tablets of the Lord of Hongnong and Gaozu were elevated to enshrinement, together with the former four chambers making six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Temple was expanded; Hongnong Lord and Gaozu were first elevated to enshrinement, bringing the shrine to six chambers.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，太宗崩，將行崇祔之禮，禮部尚書許敬宗奏言：「弘農府君廟應迭毀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Taizong died; they were about to perform the elevated-enshrinement rite. Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong memorialized, saying: "The temple of the Lord of Hongnong should be destroyed in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Year 23: Taizong died; elevated enshrinement was due. Xu Jingzong of Rites wrote: "The Hongnong Lord's temple should rotate out.

sentences.zh: 謹按舊儀，漢丞相韋玄成以為毀主瘞埋。

translations.literal: According to former rites, Han Chancellor-in-ordinary Wei Xuancheng held that destroyed spirit tablets should be buried in the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Former rites: Han Chancellor Wei Xuancheng said destroyed tablets should be buried.

sentences.zh: 但萬國宗饗，有所從來，一旦瘞埋，事不允愜。

translations.literal: Yet when the myriad states pay collective honor, there is an origin for ritual—suddenly to bury them would not be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all realms honor a lineage with roots—sudden burial would not satisfy.

sentences.zh: 晉博士范宣意欲別立廟宇，奉征西等主安置其中。

translations.literal: Jin Erudite Fan Xuan wished to establish a separate temple and place therein the spirit tablets of the Commander who Pacified the West and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Jin scholar Fan Xuan wanted a separate shrine for the Pacified-West commander and others.

sentences.zh: 方之瘞埋，頗葉情理，事無典故，亦未足依。

translations.literal: Compared with burial, this rather accords with reason, but there is no precedent and it is not sufficient to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: That beats burial in reason, but lacks precedent and cannot be followed.

sentences.zh: 又議者或言毀主藏於天府，祥瑞所藏，本非斯意。

translations.literal: Some debaters also said to store destroyed tablets in the Celestial Repository—the repository where auspicious objects were stored was not originally for this purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Others urged storing tablets in the Celestial Repository—but that treasury held omens, not ancestors.

sentences.zh: 今謹准量，去祧之外，猶有壇墠，祈禱所及，竊謂合宜。

translations.literal: We now carefully measure: beyond the distant ancestors, altars and open platforms for prayer still remain—a private opinion that this is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: We weigh the case: beyond the remote ancestors, prayer altars still stand—we deem that fitting.

sentences.zh: 今時廟制，與古不同，共基別室，西方為首。

translations.literal: The present temple system differs from antiquity: a shared foundation with separate chambers, the west taken as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Today's temples differ from antiquity—one foundation, separate chambers, west ranked first.

sentences.zh: 若在西夾之中，仍處尊位，祈禱則祭，未絕祗享，方諸舊儀，情實可安。

translations.literal: If within the western side chambers they still occupy the honored position, and prayer sacrifices are offered without ending reverent offerings, compared with former rites, sentiment and fact can both be settled.
translations.idiomatic: If western side chambers keep honored rank and prayer offerings continue, old rite and present need both align.

sentences.zh: 弘農府君廟遠親殺，詳據舊章，禮合迭毀。

translations.literal: The Hongnong lord's temple is subject to reduced mourning for distant kin; per detailed examination of old regulations, ritual requires rotational destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong Lord is a distant relation—old statutes require his temple to rotate out.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，遷奉神主，藏於夾室，本情篤教，在理為弘。

translations.literal: Your subjects jointly deliberated: moving and enshrining the spirit tablets, storing them in the side chambers—in native feeling, profound teaching; in principle, expansive.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly advise moving the tablets into side chambers—deep in piety, broad in principle.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended." Approved.

sentences.zh: 其年八月庚子，太宗文皇帝神主祔於太廟。

translations.literal: That year, eighth month, gengzi day, the spirit tablet of Emperor Wen Taizong was enshrined in the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That year, eighth month, day gengzi: Taizong's tablet entered the Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 八月，奉高宗神主祔於太廟中，始遷宣皇帝神主于夾室。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the spirit tablet of Emperor Gaozong was enshrined within the Great Temple; for the first time the spirit tablet of Emperor Xuan was moved to the side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Gaozong's tablet was enshrined; Xuan's tablet moved to the side chambers for the first time.

sentences.zh: 正月，又於東都立高祖、太宗、高宗三廟，四時享祀，如京廟之儀。

translations.literal: First month: at the eastern capital three temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were also erected; seasonal offerings followed the capital temple rite.
translations.idiomatic: First month: eastern capital gained three temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, with seasonal rites matching the capital.

sentences.zh: 別立崇先廟以享武氏祖考。

translations.literal: A separate Chongxian Temple was established to offer to the Wu clan ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: A separate Chongxian Temple was built for Wu clan ancestors.

sentences.zh: 則天尋又令所司議立崇先廟室數，司禮博士、崇文館學士周忭希旨，請立崇先廟為七室，其皇室太廟，減為五室。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian soon again ordered the offices to deliberate on how many chambers the Chongxian Temple should have; Court of Spring Rites erudite and Scholar of the Chongwen Institute Zhou Ping, to please her intent, requested seven chambers for Chongxian Temple and reduction of the imperial ancestral temple to five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian soon ordered debate on Chongxian's chamber count; Zhou Ping of Spring Rites, courting her wish, urged seven chambers for Chongxian and five for the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 春官侍郎賈大隱奏曰：「臣竊准秦、漢皇太后臨朝稱制，並據禮經正文，天子七廟，諸侯五廟。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Court of Spring Rites Jia Dayin memorialized, saying: "Your subject ventures to cite Qin and Han, when empress dowagers held court and exercised regulatory power—all followed the canonical ritual texts: the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five temples.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dayin of Spring Rites wrote: "Qin and Han dowagers who ruled from court all cited canon—the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples, lords five.

sentences.zh: 蓋百王不易之義，萬代常行之法，未有越禮違古而擅裁儀注者也。

translations.literal: This is the unchanging meaning of the hundred kings, the constant law of myriad generations—never has anyone transgressed ritual and antiquity to arrogate regulation of ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: That is the immovable rule of kings and ages—none has broken ritual to rewrite ceremony at will.

sentences.zh: 今周悰別引浮議，廣述異文，直崇臨朝權儀，不依國家常度，升崇先之廟而七，降國家之廟而五。

translations.literal: Now Zhou Cong cites floating opinions and broadly sets forth heterodox texts, directly elevating provisional rites of holding court, not relying on the state's constant norms—raising Chongxian temple to seven while lowering the state temple to five.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cong now cites loose opinion and stray texts, exalting a regent's provisional rite over state norm—seven for Chongxian, five for the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣聞皇圖廣辟，實崇宗社之尊；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: when the imperial design is broadly opened, it truly honors the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: when the throne's design is wide, the altars of state gain honor;

sentences.zh: 帝業弘基，實等山河之固。

translations.literal: when the imperial enterprise has a vast foundation, it truly equals the solidity of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: when its foundation is vast, it matches mountains and rivers in firmness.

sentences.zh: 伏以天步多艱，時逢遏密，代天理物，自古有之。

translations.literal: Your subject observes: the heavenly steps have been many times arduous; times encountered mourning seclusion; one who substitutes for Heaven and governs things has existed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's course has been hard; times of mourning seclusion came; regents who govern for Heaven are ancient.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太后親承顧托，憂勤黎庶，納孝慈之請，垂矜撫之懷，實所謂光顯大猷，恢崇聖載。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully considers: the Empress Dowager personally received the entrustment, labored in care for the common people, accepted the request of filial piety and compassion, extended a cherishing and soothing heart—this truly is what is called to glorify the great plan and expand the sage burden.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager took the trust, toiled for the people, heard pleas of filial mercy, and soothed the realm—truly glorifying the great design and widening the sage charge.

sentences.zh: 其崇先廟室，合同諸侯之數，國家宗廟，不合輒有移變。

translations.literal: Chambers of Chongxian Temple should accord with the feudal lord count; the state ancestral temple must not casually be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian should match a lord's count; the state temple must not be casually altered.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚直，並依正禮，周忭之請，實乖古儀。

translations.literal: Your subject's stubborn directness wholly follows orthodox ritual; Zhou Ping's request truly contravenes ancient ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: My blunt counsel follows orthodox rite; Zhou Ping's plea breaches ancient ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」則天由是且止。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Zetian thereby stopped for the time.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended." Zetian held off for the moment.

sentences.zh: ，則天既革命稱帝，於東都改制太廟為七廟室，奉武氏七代神主，祔於太廟。

translations.literal: When Zetian had revolutionized and taken the imperial title, at the eastern capital she reformed the Great Temple into seven temple chambers, received the spirit tablets of seven generations of the Wu clan, and enshrined them in the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After Zetian's revolution and enthronement, the eastern capital Great Temple became seven chambers; seven generations of Wu tablets were enshrined there.

sentences.zh: 改西京太廟為享德廟，四時唯享高祖已下三室，餘四室令所司閉其門，廢其享祀之禮。

translations.literal: The western capital Great Temple was changed to the Virtue-Enjoying Temple; in the four seasons only the three chambers from Gaozu downward were offered; the remaining four chambers had their doors closed by order and their offering rites abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Western capital's Great Temple became Virtue-Enjoying Temple—only three chambers from Gaozu down were offered; four chambers were closed and their rites ended.

sentences.zh: 又改西京崇先廟為崇尊廟，其享祀如太廟之儀。

translations.literal: Also the western capital Chongxian Temple was changed to Chongzun Temple; its offerings followed the Great Temple rite.
translations.idiomatic: Western Chongxian became Chongzun Temple, with rites like the Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 臘月，封嵩山回，親謁太廟。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: returning from conferring feng on Mount Song, she personally visited the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: returning from Song's feng rite, she visited the Great Temple in person.

sentences.zh: 明年七月，又改京崇尊廟，為太廟，仍改太廟署為清廟臺，加官員，崇其班秩。

translations.literal: Seventh month next year: also changed the capital Chongzun Temple back to Great Temple; still changed the Great Temple Bureau to Qingmiao Terrace, added staff, and elevated their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, seventh month: Chongzun was restored as Great Temple; the temple office became Qingmiao Terrace with added staff and higher rank.

sentences.zh: 四月，又親祀太廟，曲赦東都城內。

translations.literal: Fourth month: again personally sacrificed at the Great Temple; special amnesty within the eastern capital walls.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: she sacrificed at the Great Temple again and granted amnesty within the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，正月，改享德廟依舊為京太廟。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, first month: restored Virtue-Enjoying Temple to the capital Great Temple as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's first month: Virtue-Enjoying Temple reverted to the capital Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 五月，遷武氏七廟神主於西京之崇尊廟，東都創置太廟。

translations.literal: Fifth month: moved the seven Wu clan temple spirit tablets to western capital Chongzun Temple; newly established Great Temple at eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: seven Wu tablets went to western Chongzun; a new Great Temple rose at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 太常博士張齊賢建議曰：

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite Zhang Qixian memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices Erudite Zhang Qixian submitted:

sentences.zh: 太常博士劉承慶、尹知章又議云：

translations.literal: Erudites Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also argued:

sentences.zh: 時有制令宰相更加詳定，禮部尚書祝欽明等奏言：「博士三人，自分兩議：張齊賢以始同太祖，不合更祖昭王；

translations.literal: Then there was an edict ordering the chief ministers to deliberate further; Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming and others memorialized, saying: "Three erudites divided into two opinions: Zhang Qixian held that from the first they were the same as the Great Founder, and it was not fitting to further take King Zhao as ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent chancellors to refine the question; Zhu Qinming of Rites reported: "Three erudites split two ways—Zhang Qixian said they were already Great Founder and King Zhao should not be added as ancestor;

sentences.zh: 劉承慶以《王制》三昭三穆，不合重崇宣帝。

translations.literal: Liu Chengqing held that the Wang System's three Zhao and three Mu does not permit doubly honoring Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengqing cited the Wang System's three zhao and three mu—no double honor for Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，請依張齊賢以景皇帝為太祖，依劉承慶尊崇六室。

translations.literal: Your subjects deliberated and request: follow Zhang Qixian in taking Emperor Jing as Great Founder, follow Liu Chengqing in honoring with six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: We advise: take Zhang Qixian's Jing as Great Founder and Liu Chengqing's six-chamber arrangement.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended." Approved.

sentences.zh: 尋有制以孝敬皇帝為義宗，升祔於太廟。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict making Filial and Respectful Emperor the Righteous Ancestor, elevated enshrinement in the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict made the Filial and Respectful Emperor the Righteous Ancestor and elevated him into the Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，崇祔光皇帝、太祖景皇帝、代祖元皇帝、高祖神堯皇帝、太宗文武聖皇帝、皇考高宗天皇大帝、皇兄義宗孝敬皇帝于東都之太廟，躬行享獻之禮。

translations.literal: That year eighth month: elevated enshrinement of Emperors Guang, Jing as Great Founder, Yuan as Dynastic Ancestor, Gaozu as Emperor Shenyao, Taizong as the Civil and Martial Sage Emperor, father Emperor Gaozong the Great Heavenly Emperor, elder brother Righteous Ancestor Filial and Respectful Emperor at the eastern capital Great Temple; the emperor in person performed the offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month at the eastern Great Temple: elevated enshrinement for Guang, Jing as Great Founder, Yuan as dynastic ancestor, Shenyao Gaozu, sage Taizong, heavenly Gaozong, and Righteous Ancestor Filial and Respectful—the emperor offered in person.

sentences.zh: 二年，駕還京師，太廟自是亦崇享七室，仍改武氏崇尊廟為崇恩廟。

translations.literal: Year 2: when the carriage returned to the capital, the Great Temple from then also honored seven chambers; still changed Wu clan Chongzun Temple to Chong'en Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2: back in the capital, the Great Temple too kept seven chambers; Wu Chongzun became Chong'en Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，復令崇恩廟一依天授時享祭。

translations.literal: Second month next year: again ordered Chong'en Temple to follow Tian'shou-era offerings entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Next year's second month: Chong'en was again ordered to follow Tian'shou offerings.

sentences.zh: 時武三思用事，密令安樂公主諷中宗，故有此制。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sansi was in power; secretly ordered Princess Anle to persuade Zhongzong—hence this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi then held sway; Princess Anle quietly swayed Zhongzong—hence the edict.

sentences.zh: 尋又特令武氏崇恩廟齋郎取五品子充。

translations.literal: Soon also specially ordered Wu clan Chong'en Temple Fast Youths to be filled with sons of fifth-rank officials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wu's Chong'en Fast Youths were specially filled with fifth-rank sons.

sentences.zh: 太常博士楊孚奏言：「太廟齋郎，承前只七品已下子。

translations.literal: Erudite Yang Fu memorialized, saying: "Great Temple Fast Youths—formerly only sons of seventh rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu wrote: "Great Temple Fast Youths were formerly sons of seventh rank and below.

sentences.zh: 今崇恩廟齋郎既取五品子，即太廟齋郎作何等級？

translations.literal: Now that Chong'en Temple Fast Youths take fifth-rank sons, what rank should Great Temple Fast Youths be?"
translations.idiomatic: If Chong'en takes fifth-rank sons, what rank should Great Temple youths hold?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「太廟齋郎亦准崇恩廟置。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Great Temple Fast Youths likewise follow Chong'en Temple."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Match the Great Temple to Chong'en."

sentences.zh: 」孚奏曰：「崇恩廟為太廟之臣，太廟為崇恩廟之君，以臣准君，猶為僭逆，以君准臣，天下疑懼。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized, saying: "Chong'en Temple is subject of the Great Temple, the Great Temple is lord of Chong'en Temple—to equalize subject with lord is still usurpation; to equalize lord with subject makes the realm doubtful and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied: "Chong'en is the Great Temple's subject, the Great Temple its lord—equating subject to lord is usurpation; equating lord to subject breeds fear.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『名不正則言不順，言不順則事不成，事不成則禮樂不興，禮樂不興則刑罰不中，刑罰不中則人無所措手足。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'If names are not correct speech is not in accord; if speech is not in accord affairs do not succeed; if affairs do not succeed rites and music do not flourish; if rites and music do not flourish punishments miss the mark; if punishments miss the mark the people have nowhere to place hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'Wrong names unbalance speech; unbalanced speech fails affairs; failed affairs stall rites and music; stalled rites skew punishments; skewed punishments leave the people without footing.

sentences.zh: 故君子名之必可言也。

translations.literal: Therefore the noble man in naming must make speakable words.
translations.idiomatic: So the noble man's names must be sayable.

sentences.zh: 』伏願無惑邪言，以為亂始。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes no confusion from heterodox words as the beginning of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Do not heed crooked words and start disorder.

sentences.zh: 」其事乃寢。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended." The plan died.

sentences.zh: 崇恩廟至睿宗踐祚，乃廢毀之。

translations.literal: Chong'en Temple—when Ruizong took the throne, was then abolished and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'en lasted until Ruizong's accession, then was abolished.

sentences.zh: 冬，將葬中宗孝和皇帝于定陵，中書令姚元之、吏部尚書宋璟奏言：「准禮，大行皇帝山陵事終，即合祔廟。

translations.literal: Winter: about to bury Emperor Xiaohui of Zhongzong at Ding Mausoleum; Chief Minister Yao Yuanzhi and Minister of Personnel Song Jing memorialized, saying: "Per ritual, when the great imperial tomb matters end, enshrinement should follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: Zhongzong Xiaohui was to be buried at Ding; Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing wrote: "When the great tomb rites end, enshrinement should follow immediately.

sentences.zh: 其太廟第七室，先祔皇兄義宗孝敬皇帝、哀皇后裴氏神主。

translations.literal: The seventh chamber of the Great Temple had already enshrined the elder brother Righteous Ancestor Filial and Respectful Emperor and the Lamenting Empress Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh chamber already held Righteous Ancestor Filial and Respectful and Lamenting Empress Pei.

sentences.zh: 伏以義宗未登大位，崩後追尊，神龍之初，乃特令遷祔。

translations.literal: Your subject observes: Righteous Ancestor never ascended the great throne; posthumously honored after death—in the early Shenlong era a special order moved enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous Ancestor never reigned; he was honored after death and specially moved in early Shenlong.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，國君即位未逾年者，不合列敘昭穆。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals principle: a lord of the state who took the throne not yet a full year is not fit to be ranked in zhao and mu sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn rule: a ruler enthroned less than a year is not ranked in zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 又古者祖宗各別立廟，孝敬皇帝恭陵既在洛州，望於東都別立義宗之廟，遷祔孝敬皇帝、哀皇后神主，命有司以時享祭，則不違先旨，又協古訓，人神允穆，進退得宜。

translations.literal: Also in antiquity ancestor-for-father each had separate temples. Filial and Respectful Emperor's Gong Mausoleum is already in Luozhou—your subject requests a separate Righteous Ancestor temple at the eastern capital, moving enshrinement of Filial and Respectful Emperor and Lamenting Empress spirit tablets, ordering the relevant office seasonal offerings—then not violating the prior intent, also harmonizing with ancient instruction; human and spirit both agree; advance and retreat all fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity gave each forebear a separate temple. Filial and Respectful lies at Gong in Luozhou—build a Righteous Ancestor temple in the east, move both tablets, and offer by season: prior intent kept, ancient rule met, spirits and men aligned.

sentences.zh: 在此神主，望入夾室安置。

translations.literal: These spirit tablets—your subject requests placement in side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Place these tablets in the side chambers.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下以禮斷恩。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to cut favor with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Let ritual trim private favor.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended." Approved.

sentences.zh: 及既葬，祔中宗孝和皇帝、和思皇后趙氏神主於太廟。

translations.literal: When burial was done, enshrined spirit tablets of Emperor Xiaohui Zhongzong and Empress Zhaosi Zhao in the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After burial, Zhongzong Xiaohui and Empress Zhaosi Zhao were enshrined in the Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 其義宗即於東都從善裏建廟享祀。

translations.literal: Righteous Ancestor was then at eastern capital Congshan Lane with temple established for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous Ancestor was served at a new temple in Congshan Lane, eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 時又追尊昭成、肅明二皇后，于親仁裏別置儀坤廟，四時享祭。

translations.literal: At the time also posthumously honored Empresses Zhaocheng and Suming; at Qinren Lane a separate Yikun Temple was set up with four-season offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Zhaocheng and Suming were also posthumously honored; Yikun Temple at Qinren Lane received seasonal rites.

sentences.zh: ，睿宗崩，及行祔廟之禮，太常博士陳貞節、蘇獻等奏議曰：「謹按孝和皇帝在廟，七室已滿。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, and enshrinement rites were performed, Erudites Chen Zhenjie, Su Xian and others deliberated, saying: "According to examination, Emperor Xiaohui in the temple—seven chambers already full.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong's death brought enshrinement debate; Chen Zhenjie and Su Xian wrote: "Xiaohui already fills seven chambers.

sentences.zh: 今睿宗大聖真皇帝是孝和之弟，甫及仲冬，禮當祔遷。

translations.literal: Now Emperor Ruizong the Great Sagely True Emperor is Xiaohui's younger brother—just reaching mid-winter, ritual requires enshrinement migration.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong the Great Sagely True Emperor is Xiaohui's younger brother—mid-winter demands his enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 但兄弟入廟，古則有焉，遞遷之禮，昭穆須正。

translations.literal: Though brothers entering the temple existed in antiquity, the rite of successive removal—zhao and mu must be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers did enter temples in antiquity, but succession rules require correct zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 謹按《禮論》，太常賀循議云：『兄弟不相為後也。

translations.literal: According to Treatises on Ritual, Imperial Sacrifices Officer He Xun's deliberation: 'Brothers do not succeed one another as heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual treatises cite He Xun: 'Brothers do not succeed one another.

sentences.zh: 故殷之盤庚，不序于陽甲，而上繼於先君；

translations.literal: Hence Yin Pan Geng is not ranked after Yang Jia but succeeds the former lord above;
translations.idiomatic: Yin's Pan Geng is not listed after Yang Jia but continues the prior lord;

sentences.zh: 漢之光武，不嗣于孝成，而上承於元帝。

translations.literal: Han Guangwu does not succeed Xiaocheng but receives above from Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Guangwu does not follow Xiaocheng but inherits from Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『晉惠帝無後，懷帝承統，懷帝自繼于世祖，而不繼于惠帝。

translations.literal: ' Also: 'Jin Emperor Hui had no heir; Emperor Huai received the succession; Huai succeeded himself from Shizu, not from Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: ' Jin Hui had no heir; Huai took the line from Shizu, not from Hui.

sentences.zh: 其惠帝當同陽甲、孝成，別出為廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui should be the same as Yang Jia and Xiaocheng, separately enshrined outside.
translations.idiomatic: Hui should join Yang Jia and Xiaocheng in a separate shrine.

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『若兄弟相代，則共是一代，昭穆位同。

translations.literal: ' Also: 'If brothers replace one another, they share one generation; zhao and mu positions identical.
translations.idiomatic: ' If brothers alternate, they share one generation and one zhao-mu slot.

sentences.zh: 至其當遷，不可兼毀二廟。

translations.literal: 'When they should be removed, two temples cannot both be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: ' When rotation comes, two temples cannot both be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 』此蓋禮之常例也。

translations.literal: ' This is the constant example of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: ' That is ritual's standing rule.

sentences.zh: 《荀卿子》曰，『有天下者事七代』，謂從禰已上也。

translations.literal: Xunzi says, 'He who has the realm serves seven generations'—meaning from honored father upward.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi: 'He who holds the realm serves seven generations'—from honored father up.

sentences.zh: 尊者統廣，故恩及遠祖。

translations.literal: The honored unify broadly, hence grace extends to distant ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The exalted reach wide, so grace reaches distant forebears.

sentences.zh: 若旁容兄弟，上毀祖考，此則天子有不得全事於七代之義矣。

translations.literal: If brothers are admitted laterally, destroying ancestor-fathers above—then the Son of Heaven has the meaning of being unable fully to serve seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: Admit brothers sideways and remove ancestors above—the Son of Heaven cannot fully keep seven generations.

sentences.zh: 孝和皇帝有中興之功，而無後嗣，請同殷之陽甲、漢之成帝，出為別廟，時祭不虧，大祫之辰，合食太祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui had merit of restoring the dynasty but no posterity—your subject requests the same as Yin Yang Jia, Han Emperor Cheng: separate temple outside, seasonal rites not diminished; at great he sacrifice, joint feast at Great Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohui restored the dynasty but left no heir—treat him like Yang Jia and Cheng: separate temple, unbroken seasonal rites, joint feast at the Great Founder on great he days.

sentences.zh: 奉睿宗神主升祔太廟，上繼高宗，則昭穆永貞，獻祼長序。

translations.literal: Receive Emperor Ruizong's spirit tablet, elevated enshrinement in Great Temple, succeeding above Emperor Gaozong—then zhao and mu forever stable, libation and blessing long in order.
translations.idiomatic: Enshrine Ruizong above Gaozong—zhao and mu stay fixed, libations and blessings in long order.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended." Approved.

sentences.zh: 初令以儀坤廟為中宗廟，尋又改造中宗廟於太廟之西。

translations.literal: Initially ordered Yikun Temple to become Zhongzong's temple; soon again reformed Zhongzong Temple west of the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yikun was first made Zhongzong's temple, then Zhongzong's shrine was rebuilt west of the Great Temple.

sentences.zh: 貞節等又以肅明皇后不合與昭成皇后配祔睿宗，奏議曰：「禮，宗廟父昭子穆，皆有配座，每室一帝一后，禮之正儀。

translations.literal: Zhenjie and others also held that Empress Suming was not fit to be paired with Empress Zhaocheng in enshrinement with Ruizong; deliberated, saying: "Ritual: ancestral temples father-zhao son-mu—each has a consort seat; each chamber one emperor one empress—the orthodox ritual form.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjie et al. also argued Suming should not pair with Zhaocheng at Ruizong's shrine: "Rite sets father-zhao, son-mu, one consort per chamber—one emperor, one empress: the orthodox form.

sentences.zh: 自夏、殷而來，無易茲典。

translations.literal: From Xia and Yin down, this statute has not been changed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xia and Yin, this institution has never been altered.

sentences.zh: 伏惟昭成皇后，有太姒之德，已配食于睿宗；

translations.literal: We humbly note: Empress Zhaocheng had the virtue of Tai Si and already shares sacrifice in Ruizong's chamber;
translations.idiomatic: It is submitted that Empress Zhaocheng possessed Tai Si's virtue and already shares sacrifice with Ruizong;

sentences.zh: 則肅明皇后無啟母之尊，自應別立一廟。

translations.literal: then Empress Suming lacked the standing of Qi's mother and ought on her own to have a separate temple established.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Empress Suming did not have Qi's mother's rank and should have a temple of her own.

sentences.zh: 謹按《周禮》云『奏夷則，歌小呂，以享先妣』者，姜嫄是也。

translations.literal: We respectfully cite the Zhou Rites: "Play Yi ze, sing Xiao lü, to offer to the former consort"—that is Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Rites state that playing Yi ze and singing Xiao lü to honor a former consort refers to Jiang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 姜嫄是帝嚳之妃，后稷之母，特為立廟，名曰閟宮。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuan was consort of Emperor Ku and mother of Hou Ji; a temple was specially established for her, named Bi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan was Emperor Ku's consort and Hou Ji's mother; she was given a separate temple called Bi Palace.

sentences.zh: 又《禮論》云，晉伏系之議云：『晉簡文鄭宣后既不配食，乃築宮於外，歲時就廟享祭而已。

translations.literal: Also the Ritual Disquisitions says Fu Xi's discussion of Jin states: "Empress Xuande of Jin Emperor Jianwen, since she was not allotted shared sacrifice, built a palace outside; at the seasons one went to the temple to offer sacrifice only.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Disquisitions also cites Fu Xi on Jin: when Empress Xuande of Emperor Jianwen was denied shared sacrifice, a palace was built outside and seasonal offerings were made there alone.

sentences.zh: 』今肅明皇后無祔配之位，請同姜嫄、宣后，別廟而處，四時享祭如舊儀。

translations.literal: " Now Empress Suming has no position for complementary enshrinement; we ask, following Jiang Yuan and Empress Xuande, to have a separate temple and placement, the four seasons' sacrifices as the old observances."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Suming likewise has no place for enshrinement; we ask that she, like Jiang Yuan and Empress Xuande, have a separate temple with seasonal sacrifices as before."

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: The decree followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 於是遷昭成皇后神主祔于睿宗之室，惟留肅明神主於儀坤廟。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tablet of Empress Zhaocheng was moved to share sacrifice in Ruizong's chamber; only the tablet of Suming was left in Yikun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The tablet of Empress Zhaocheng was then moved to Ruizong's chamber, leaving only Suming's tablet in Yikun Temple.

sentences.zh: 時太常卿姜皎復與禮官上表曰：「臣聞敬宗尊祖，享德崇恩，必也正名，用光時憲，禮也。

translations.literal: At that time Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao again, with ritual officials, submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that revering the clan and honoring ancestors, enjoying virtue and exalting grace, must rectify names to illuminate the statutes of the age—this is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Director Jiang Jiao and the ritual officials again memorialized: "We hear that revering ancestors and exalting grace require correct titles to honor the age's laws—that is ritual.

sentences.zh: 伏見太廟中則天皇后配高宗天皇大帝，題云『天后聖帝武氏』。

translations.literal: We note in the Grand Temple Empress Zetian is enshrined with Emperor Gaozong Tianhuang Dadi, the inscription reading "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Temple Empress Zetian shares sacrifice with Emperor Gaozong, inscribed as "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."

sentences.zh: 伏尋昔居寵秩，親承顧托，因攝大政，事乃從權。

translations.literal: We trace how in the past she held favored rank and personally received the entrustment; she then assumed great government, the affair being one of expedient power.
translations.idiomatic: She once held favored rank, received the late emperor's trust, and took power as an expedient measure.

sentences.zh: 神龍之初，已去帝號。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong the imperial title was already removed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong her imperial title had already been removed.

sentences.zh: 岑羲等不閑政體，復題帝名。

translations.literal: Cen Xi and others were unversed in the body of government and again inscribed an imperial name.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Xi and others, ignorant of governance, restored an imperial title on the inscription.

sentences.zh: 若又使帝號長存，恐非聖朝通典。

translations.literal: If the imperial title is again made to endure long, I fear it is not the general statute of the sagely court.
translations.idiomatic: To let an imperial title stand again would violate court precedent.

sentences.zh: 夫七廟者，高祖神堯皇帝之廟也。

translations.literal: The seven temples are the temples of the High Ancestor, the Divine Yao Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The seven temples are those of the High Ancestor, Emperor Shen Yao.

sentences.zh: 父昭子穆，祖德宗功，非夫帝子天孫，乘乾出震者，不得升祔於斯矣。

translations.literal: Father zhao, son mu; ancestral virtue and clan achievement—none but sons of emperors and grandsons of Heaven, those who mount Qian and issue from Zhen, may ascend to enshrinement there.
translations.idiomatic: Father-zhao, son-mu, ancestral merit—only imperial sons and heaven's grandsons who received the mandate may be enshrined there.

sentences.zh: 但皇后祔廟，配食高宗，位號舊章，無宜稱帝。

translations.literal: But the empress enshrined in the temple, sharing sacrifice with Gaozong, by old title and statute ought not be called emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as consort sharing Gaozong's sacrifices, her old titles should not include "emperor."

sentences.zh: 今山陵日近，陞祔非遙，請申陳告之儀，因除『聖帝』之字，直題云『則天皇后武氏』。

translations.literal: Now the imperial tomb day draws near and ascent to enshrinement is not distant; we ask to declare the announcement rite and remove the words "Holy Emperor," inscribing simply "Empress Zetian Wu."
translations.idiomatic: With her enshrinement near, we ask to perform the announcement rite, drop "Holy Emperor," and inscribe only "Empress Zetian Wu."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時既另造義宗廟，將作大匠韋湊上疏曰：「臣聞王者制體，是曰規模；

translations.literal: At that time a separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the king establishes the body—this is called the model;
translations.idiomatic: A separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou wrote: "A king's institutions are his model;

sentences.zh: 規模之興，實資師古；

translations.literal: the rise of the model in fact relies on taking antiquity as teacher;
translations.idiomatic: and models must learn from antiquity;

sentences.zh: 師古之道，必也正名；

translations.literal: the Way of taking antiquity as teacher must rectify names;
translations.idiomatic: which requires correct names;

sentences.zh: 惟名與實，固當相副。

translations.literal: names and reality solidly ought to match each other.
translations.idiomatic: name and fact must agree.

sentences.zh: 其在宗廟，禮之大者，豈可失哉！

translations.literal: As for the ancestral temple, the greatest of rites—how can it be lost!
translations.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple, the greatest rite—how can it be neglected!

sentences.zh: 禮，祖有功而宗有德。

translations.literal: Ritual: the ancestor has merit, the clan lord has virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual holds that ancestors have merit and clan lords have virtue.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之廟，百代不毀。

translations.literal: The temples of ancestor and clan lord are not destroyed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor and clan-lord temples stand for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 故殷太甲曰太宗，太戊曰中宗，武丁曰高宗。

translations.literal: Thus Yin's Tai Jia was called Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, Wu Ding Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's Tai Jia was styled Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, and Wu Ding Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 周宗文王、武王。

translations.literal: Zhou honored King Wen and King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou honored Kings Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 漢則文帝為太宗，武帝為世宗。

translations.literal: Han made Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Han styled Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.

sentences.zh: 其後代有稱宗，皆以方制海內，德澤可宗，列于昭穆，期於不毀。

translations.literal: Afterward generations had those styled "zong," all because they regulated the realm within the four seas and their virtue and grace could be honored; ranked in zhao and mu, they were expected not to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers styled "zong" when their virtue filled the realm and merited lasting place in the zhao-mu sequence.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之義，不亦大乎！

translations.literal: The meaning of ancestor and clan lord—is it not great!
translations.idiomatic: The weight of "ancestor" and "zong" is immense.

sentences.zh: 況孝敬皇帝位止東宮，未嘗南面，聖道誠冠于儲副，德教不被於寰瀛，立廟稱宗，恐非合體。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Xiaojing's position stopped at the Eastern Palace; he never faced south. His sagely Way indeed topped the heir, yet his moral teaching did not spread through the realm—establishing a temple and styling him zong, I fear, is not fitting the body of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing never ruled; though his virtue surpassed other heirs, his teaching did not reach the realm—calling him "zong" does not fit ritual.

sentences.zh: 況別起寢廟，不入昭穆，稽諸祀典，何義稱宗？

translations.literal: Moreover a separate sleeping temple was raised, not entering zhao and mu; searching the sacrifice canon, what meaning is there in calling him zong?
translations.idiomatic: A separate shrine outside the zhao-mu line cannot be called "zong" under the sacrifice canon.

sentences.zh: 而廟號義宗，稱之萬代。

translations.literal: Yet the temple name Yizong would be spoken for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the temple name Yizong would stand for ages.

sentences.zh: 以臣庸識，竊謂不可。

translations.literal: By your servant's shallow knowledge, I privately deem it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 望更令有司詳定，務合於禮。

translations.literal: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Please have the offices review this and align it with ritual.

sentences.zh: 」於是太常請以本諡「孝敬」為廟稱。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices asked to use his posthumous title "Xiaojing" as the temple designation.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices then proposed his posthumous title Xiaojing as the temple name.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，玄宗將行幸東都，而太廟屋壞，乃奉七廟神主於太極殿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Xuanzong was about to travel to the eastern capital, but the Grand Temple buildings collapsed; he therefore moved the seven temples' tablets to Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's first month Xuanzong planned to visit the eastern capital; when the Grand Temple collapsed, he moved all seven tablets to Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 玄宗素服避正殿，輟朝三日，親謁神主於太極殿，而後發幸東都。

translations.literal: Xuanzong wore plain dress and avoided the main hall, halted court for three days, personally visited the tablets in Taiji Hall, and afterward set out for the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He wore mourning dress, avoided the main hall, suspended court for three days, visited the tablets in Taiji Hall, then traveled east.

sentences.zh: 乃敕有司修太廟。

translations.literal: He then ordered the relevant offices to repair the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered repairs to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年，廟成，玄宗還京，行親祔之禮。

translations.literal: The next year the temple was completed; Xuanzong returned to the capital and performed the rite of personal complementary enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was finished the next year, he returned and performed the enshrinement rite in person.

sentences.zh: 時有司撰儀注，以祔祭之日車駕發宮中，玄宗謂宋璟、蘇頲曰：「」璟等稱聖情深至，請即奉行。

translations.literal: When the relevant offices drafted observances, on the day of complementary sacrifice the imperial carriage was to set out from within the palace. Xuanzong said to Song Jing and Su Ting: "Rites require fasting first, to align the mind. Per the observances, on the day of sacrifice the carriage sets out from Daming Palace, and the rite is performed at dawn; even if one sets out before the stars fade, one still arrives only after the hour has shifted—how can a dawn rite be kept? Moreover I dare not lodge in the fasting palace yet rest in the main hall. A fasting palace should be set up at the temple; on the fifth day go to the traveling palace to keep fast, on the sixth perform the rite at dawn—then it may accord with ritual." Jing and the rest praised the sagely feeling as profound and utmost, and asked to carry it out at once.
translations.idiomatic: The offices drafted rites requiring the emperor to leave the palace on the enshrinement day. Xuanzong told Song Jing and Su Ting: "Rites require fasting first, to align the mind. Per the observances, on the day of sacrifice the carriage sets out from Daming Palace, and the rite is performed at dawn; even if one sets out before the stars fade, one still arrives only after the hour has shifted—how can a dawn rite be kept? Moreover I dare not lodge in the fasting palace yet rest in the main hall. A fasting palace should be set up at the temple; on the fifth day go to the traveling palace to keep fast, on the sixth perform the rite at dawn—then it may accord with ritual." They praised his devotion and asked to follow the revised plan immediately.

sentences.zh: 詔有司改定儀注。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to revise the observances.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the rites revised.

sentences.zh: 六日，玄宗自齋宮步詣太廟，入自東門，就立位。

translations.literal: On the sixth day Xuanzong on foot went from the fasting palace to the Grand Temple, entered by the east gate, and took his standing position.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day he walked from the fasting palace to the Grand Temple, entered the east gate, and took his place.

sentences.zh: 樂奏九成，陞自阼階，行祼獻之禮。

translations.literal: Music played the Nine Completes; he ascended the eastern steps and performed the libation and offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Completes were played; he ascended the east steps and offered libation.

sentences.zh: 至睿宗室，俯伏鳴咽，侍臣莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Reaching Ruizong's chamber, he bowed prostrate and sobbed; attendants all wept.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruizong's chamber he prostrated himself and wept, and his attendants wept with him.

sentences.zh: 有河南府人孫平子詣闕上言：「中宗孝和皇帝既承大統，不合遷於別廟。

translations.literal: A man of Henan prefecture, Sun Pingzi, came to the gate and stated: "Emperor Xiaojing of Zhongzong, having succeeded the great succession, ought not be moved to a separate temple."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Pingzi of Henan memorialized: "Emperor Xiaojing of Zhongzong succeeded the throne and should not be kept in a separate temple."

sentences.zh: 」玄宗令宰相召平子與禮官對定可否，太常博士蘇獻等固執前議。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered the chancellor to summon Pingzi and the ritual officials to settle whether it was permissible; Court of Imperial Sacrifices Academician Su Xian and others stubbornly held to the prior discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had the chancellor convene Pingzi and the ritualists; Su Xian and others clung to the earlier decision.

sentences.zh: 平子口辯，所引咸有經據，獻等不能屈。

translations.literal: Pingzi was sharp in debate; what he cited all had canonical basis—Xian and the rest could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzi argued forcefully with scriptural citations the ritualists could not refute.

sentences.zh: 時蘇頲知政事，以獻是其從祖之兄，頗党助之，平子之議竟不得行。

translations.literal: At that time Su Ting held government affairs; because Xian was his elder cousin's brother, he quite factionally aided him, and Pingzi's discussion in the end could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ting, then in power, favored his cousin Su Xian, and Pingzi's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 平子論竟不已，遂謫平子為康州都城尉，仍差使領送至任，不許東西。

translations.literal: Pingzi's discussion did not cease; he was then demoted to metropolitan magistrate of Kang prefecture, still sent under escort to his post, not permitted east or west.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingzi persisted, he was exiled as magistrate of Kang and escorted to his post under guard.

sentences.zh: 平子之任，尋卒。

translations.literal: Pingzi on taking up his post soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after arriving.

sentences.zh: 時雖貶平子，議者深以其言為是。

translations.literal: Though Pingzi was demoted at the time, discussants deeply took his words as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his punishment, most officials thought him right.

sentences.zh: 至十年正月，下制曰：「」

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year an edict stated: "I have heard that kings take the times to establish teaching and shape ritual according to affairs; modification and preservation take fitness as root, selection and rejection take timeliness as foremost. Thus the way of increase and decrease has distinctions, and the use of substance and ornament differs. Moreover utmost virtue is called filial piety, whereby one reaches the spirits; the great affair is sacrifice, whereby one reverence the ancestral temple. The state holds the calendar and mandate, repeated glory and heaped splendor; the four quarters take their succession from its illumination, and seven generations can display its virtue. I inherit and guard the great enterprise, reverently uphold the sagely design, always mindful of bright service, never failing in sacrifice. I have reviewed the classics and inquired into old institutions: far off, Xia and Yin differed in affairs; near at hand, Han and Jin differed in the Way. Though ritual texts are not one, solemn reverence is not two. I hold that to establish love beginning with kin teaches people harmony; to establish respect beginning with elders teaches people order. Thus I lead by ritual and follow feeling; sometimes teaching is preserved in the Way, sometimes ritual follows the times. I will create institutions according to fitness—how can I be bound by antiquity and limited to today? Moreover as affection diminishes with descent in mourning grades, temples are abolished with removal and destruction. Though one looks to ancient instruction and ritual is not violated, yet when I speak forever of filial thought, feeling is not yet satisfied. Seasonal offerings then stop—how can love and honor be complete in ritual? Having prayers yet sacrificing is not virtue overflowing in lasting transmission. The removed chambers should be ranked as main chambers, so kin is not exhausted yet distant is not abolished; the temple preserves the appearance, the ancestor is still honored in establishment. Thus the four seasons may be offered without gap for destroyed tablets; for a hundred generations without removal, not only at the founding temple. This is called changing to fit ritual, acting to hit the center; the solemn matching rite can be exalted, the dignified harmony is here. Moreover brother succeeding brother has clear text in antiquity. Now Zhongzong's tablet still dwells in a separate place; searching the old facts, the court is not at ease—move it to the main temple to display the great canon. Still create nine chambers; order the relevant offices to choose a day, announce, and move."
