sentences.zh: 十一年春，玄宗還京師，下制曰：「」於是追尊宣皇帝為獻祖，復列於正室，光皇帝為懿祖，並還中宗神主於太廟。

translations.literal: In spring of the eleventh year Xuanzong returned to the capital and issued an edict: "To exalt and build the ancestral temple is the greatest of rites; to pursue filial sacrifice is the utmost of virtue. Now the ancestor is established to honor, kin have no removal order; ever mindful of solemn matching, utmost purity is applied; rafters and beams are exalted, libation and offering are then bestowed. Looking on this slight virtue, I have received the suburban sacrifice—not personally, not in person—how can I display sincere reverence? The nineteenth day of the eighth month should be used to reverently behold the nine chambers." Thereupon Xuandi was posthumously honored as Xianzu and again ranked in the main chamber; Guangdi as Yizu; and Zhongzong's tablet was also returned to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Xuanzong returned and decreed: "To exalt and build the ancestral temple is the greatest of rites; to pursue filial sacrifice is the utmost of virtue. Now the ancestor is established to honor, kin have no removal order; ever mindful of solemn matching, utmost purity is applied; rafters and beams are exalted, libation and offering are then bestowed. Looking on this slight virtue, I have received the suburban sacrifice—not personally, not in person—how can I display sincere reverence? The nineteenth day of the eighth month should be used to reverently behold the nine chambers." Xuandi was then honored as Xianzu in the main hall, Guangdi as Yizu, and Zhongzong's tablet was restored to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 及將親祔，會雨而止。

translations.literal: When he was about to perform personal complementary enshrinement, rain stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Rain halted the planned personal enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 乃令所司行事。

translations.literal: He then ordered the relevant offices to perform the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He had the offices carry out the rite instead.

sentences.zh: 其京師中宗舊廟，便毀拆之。

translations.literal: The old Zhongzong temple in the capital was then torn down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's former capital temple was demolished.

sentences.zh: 東都舊廟，始移孝敬神主祔焉。

translations.literal: In the eastern capital's old temple, the tablet of Xiaojing was first moved to complementary enshrinement there.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojing's tablet was first enshrined in the eastern capital's old temple.

sentences.zh: 其從善裏孝敬舊廟，亦令毀拆。

translations.literal: The old Xiaojing temple in Congshan Lane was also ordered demolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaojing shrine in Congshan Lane was also torn down.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，玄宗又特令遷肅明皇后神主祔于睿宗之室，仍以舊儀坤廟為肅明觀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Xuanzong again specially ordered the tablet of Empress Suming moved to share sacrifice in Ruizong's chamber; the old Yikun Temple was still made the Suming Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one he moved Suming's tablet to Ruizong's chamber and converted Yikun Temple into Suming Abbey.

sentences.zh: 十月，代宗神主將祔，禮儀使顏真卿以元皇帝代數已遠，准禮合祧，請遷於西夾室。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, as Emperor Daizong's tablet was about to be enshrined, Director of Ritual Yan Zhenqing, because the Yuan Emperor's generations were already distant, per ritual ought to be removed, and asked to move him to the western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong's tablet was to be installed, Yan Zhenqing argued that the Yuan Emperor was too remote by generation and should be moved to the western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 其奏議曰：

translations.literal: His memorial stated:
translations.idiomatic: His memorial read:

sentences.zh: ，升祔玄宗、肅宗，則獻祖、懿祖已從迭毀。

translations.literal: , when Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined, Xianzu and Yizu had already undergone successive removal.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined, Xianzu and Yizu had already been removed in turn.

sentences.zh: 伏以代宗睿文孝皇帝卒哭而祔，則合上遷一室。

translations.literal: We note Emperor Daizong the Filial, at the end of wailing and enshrinement, ought to move up one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong's enshrinement after mourning requires shifting one chamber upward.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝代數已遠，其神主准禮當祧，至禘祫之時，然後享祀。

translations.literal: The Yuan Emperor's generations are already distant; his tablet per ritual should be removed; at the di and cha rites he would then be offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Emperor is too remote; his tablet should be removed and honored only at the great di and cha sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 於是祧元皇帝于西夾室，祔代宗神主焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Yuan Emperor was removed to the western side chamber and Daizong's tablet was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Emperor was moved to the western side chamber and Daizong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 十一月，德宗神主將祔，禮儀使杜黃裳與禮官王涇等請遷高宗神主於西夾室。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, as Emperor Dezong's tablet was about to be enshrined, Director of Ritual Du Huangchang and ritual officials Wang Jing and others asked to move Gaozong's tablet to the western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong's tablet was to be installed, Du Huangchang and Wang Jing proposed moving Gaozong to the western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 其議曰：「自漢、魏已降，沿革不同。

translations.literal: Their discussion stated: "From Han and Wei down, institutions differ.
translations.idiomatic: They argued: "Since Han and Wei, practice has varied.

sentences.zh: 古者祖有功，宗有德，皆不毀之名也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the ancestor had merit and the clan lord had virtue—both are names not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity held that meritorious ancestors and virtuous clan lords were never removed.

sentences.zh: 自東漢、魏、晉，迄于陳、隋，漸違經意，子孫以推美為先，光武已下，皆有祖宗之號。

translations.literal: From Eastern Han, Wei, and Jin through Chen and Sui, they gradually departed from the classic intent; descendants took extolling beauty as foremost; from Guangwu down all had ancestor-and-clan-lord designations.
translations.idiomatic: From Eastern Han through Sui, courts increasingly praised forebears for flattery; after Guangwu nearly every emperor received "ancestor" or "zong" titles.

sentences.zh: 故至於迭毀親盡，禮亦迭遷，國家九廟之尊，皆法周制。

translations.literal: Thus when successive removal exhausted kin, ritual also shifted in turn; the state's nine temples' honor all follow Zhou's system.
translations.idiomatic: As kinship lapsed, tablets were removed in turn; the nine-temple system follows Zhou.

sentences.zh: 伏以太祖景皇帝受命于天，始封元本，德同周之后稷也。

translations.literal: We note the Great Ancestor Emperor Jing received the mandate from Heaven, first enfeoffed the primal root—his virtue equals Zhou's Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Great Ancestor Jing received Heaven's mandate and founded the line, like Zhou's Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝國朝首祚，萬葉所承，德同周之文王也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor Emperor Shen Yao was the dynasty's first reign, the myriad leaves' inheritance—his virtue equals Zhou's King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Shen Yao began the dynasty, like Zhou's King Wen.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝應天靖亂，垂統立極，德同周武王也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong the Cultural responded to Heaven, quelled disorder, and handed down the succession—his virtue equals Zhou's King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong pacified the realm and established the succession, like Zhou's King Wu.

sentences.zh: 周人郊后稷而祖文王、宗武王，聖唐郊景皇帝、祖高祖而宗太宗，皆在不遷之典。

translations.literal: Zhou in the suburbs honored Hou Ji and in the temple took King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as clan lord; sagely Tang in the suburbs honors Emperor Jing and in the temple takes the High Ancestor as ancestor and Taizong as clan lord—all in the canon of non-removal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sacrificed to Hou Ji and honored Wen and Wu in the temple; Tang sacrifices to Jing, with Shen Yao as ancestor and Taizong as zong—all never removed.

sentences.zh: 高宗皇帝今在三昭三穆之外，謂之親盡，新主入廟，禮合迭遷，藏於從西第一夾室，每至禘祫之月，合食如常。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong is now outside the three zhao and three mu—called kin exhausted; with a new tablet entering the temple, ritual requires successive removal, stored in the first side chamber from the west; each di and cha month he is jointly offered as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong now stands outside the zhao-mu line; when Dezong enters, Gaozong should move to the westernmost side chamber and still share in di and cha offerings.

sentences.zh: 」於是祧高宗神主於西夾室，祔德宗神主焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gaozong's tablet was removed to the western side chamber and Dezong's tablet was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was moved to the western side chamber and Dezong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 七月，順宗神主將祔，有司疑於遷毀，太常博士王涇建議曰：

translations.literal: In the seventh month, as Emperor Shunzong's tablet was about to be enshrined, the relevant offices were doubtful about removal and destruction; Court of Imperial Sacrifices Academician Wang Jing submitted a proposal, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong's tablet was to be installed, the offices debated removal; Academician Wang Jing proposed:

sentences.zh: 是月二十四日，禮儀使杜黃裳奏曰：「順宗皇帝神主已升祔太廟，告祧之後，即合遞遷。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of that month Director of Ritual Du Huangchang memorialized: "Emperor Shunzong's tablet has already ascended to complementary enshrinement in the Grand Temple; after announcing removal, it should shift in turn.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth Du Huangchang reported: "Shunzong is already in the Grand Temple; after the removal announcement his predecessors should shift.

sentences.zh: 中宗皇帝神主，今在三昭三穆之外，准禮合遷於太廟從西第一夾室，每至禘祫之日，合食如常。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong's tablet is now outside the three zhao and three mu; per ritual he should be moved to the Grand Temple's first side chamber from the west; on each di and cha day he is jointly offered as usual."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's tablet is outside the zhao-mu line and should move to the first western side chamber, sharing di and cha offerings as before."

sentences.zh: 」於是祧中宗神主於西夾室，祔順宗神主焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongzong's tablet was removed to the western side chamber and Shunzong's tablet was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was moved to the western side chamber and Shunzong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 有司先是以山陵將畢，議遷廟之禮。

translations.literal: The relevant offices had earlier, because the imperial tomb was nearing completion, discussed the rite of temple removal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the imperial tomb neared completion, the offices had debated temple removal.

sentences.zh: 有司以中宗為中興之君，當百代不遷之位。

translations.literal: The relevant offices took Zhongzong as a restoration ruler and entitled to the position not removed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: They argued Zhongzong was a restoration emperor who should never be removed.

sentences.zh: 宰臣召史官蔣武問之，武對曰：「中宗以于高宗柩前即位，時春秋已壯矣。

translations.literal: The chancellor summoned historiographer Jiang Wu to question him; Wu replied: "Zhongzong succeeded at Gaozong's coffin; by then his years were already mature.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor asked historiographer Jiang Wu, who replied: "Zhongzong took the throne at Gaozong's death when already mature.

sentences.zh: 及母后篡奪，神器潛移。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager usurped, the sacred vessel shifted in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager seized power, the throne was lost.

sentences.zh: 其後賴張柬之等同謀，國祚再復。

translations.literal: Afterward, relying on Zhang Jianzhi and others in common plot, the imperial fortune was twice restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Jianzhi and his allies restored him—twice.

sentences.zh: 此蓋同於反正，恐不得號為中興之君。

translations.literal: This is roughly like a return to correctness; I fear he may not be styled a restoration ruler.
translations.idiomatic: That resembles mere restoration, not the "restoration emperor" of ritual theory.

sentences.zh: 凡非我失之，自我復之，謂之中興，漢光武、晉元帝是也。

translations.literal: What is not lost by oneself but restored by oneself is called restoration—Han Guangwu and Jin Yuandi are cases.
translations.idiomatic: True restoration means regaining what one lost oneself, as with Guangwu or Jin's Yuandi.

sentences.zh: 自我失之，因人復之，晉孝惠、孝安是也。

translations.literal: What is lost by oneself but restored through others—Jin's Emperor Hui and Emperor An are cases.
translations.idiomatic: Losing the throne and recovering it through others, as with Jin's Hui and An, is different.

sentences.zh: 今中宗于惠、安二帝事同，即不可為不遷之主也。

translations.literal: Now Zhongzong's affair is the same as the two emperors Hui and An; he cannot be a ruler not removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong matches Hui and An and cannot be a permanently enshrined ruler.

sentences.zh: 」有司又云：「五王有再安社稷之功，今若遷中宗廟，則五王永絕配享之例。

translations.literal: The relevant offices also said: "The Five Kings had the achievement of twice settling the altars of soil and grain; if Zhongzong's temple is now moved, the Five Kings will forever cut off the precedent of shared sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The offices added: "Moving Zhongzong would end the Five Kings' shared sacrifice forever."

sentences.zh: 」武曰：凡配享功臣，每至禘祫年方合食太廟，居常即無享禮。

translations.literal: Wu said: Generally meritorious ministers sharing sacrifice only at di and cha years jointly eat in the Grand Temple; in ordinary times there is no offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: Wu replied: Merit-sharing ministers are fed in the Grand Temple only at di and cha; otherwise they receive no regular offerings.

sentences.zh: 今遷中宗神主，而禘祫之年，毀廟之主並陳於太廟，此同五王配食，與前時如一也。

translations.literal: Now moving Zhongzong's tablet—in di and cha years, destroyed-temple rulers are all arrayed in the Grand Temple; this is the same as the Five Kings' shared sacrifice, as before.
translations.idiomatic: Moving Zhongzong still leaves the Five Kings honored at di and cha when removed rulers are assembled—no change for them.

sentences.zh: 」有司不能答。

translations.literal: The relevant offices could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The offices had no reply.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月，禮部侍郎李建奏上大行皇帝諡曰聖神章武孝皇帝，廟號憲宗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year, Vice Minister of Rites Li Jian memorialized the late emperor's posthumous title as Emperor Sheng Shen Zhang Wu Xiao and temple name Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year Li Jian proposed the posthumous title Sheng Shen Zhang Wu Xiao and temple name Xianzong for the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，河南節度使李夷簡上議曰：「王者祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: Earlier, Military Commissioner of Henan Li Yijian had submitted a discussion, saying: "Kings take as ancestor those with merit and as clan lord those with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Yijian of Henan had argued: "Kings honor meritorious ancestors and virtuous clan lords.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝戡翦寇逆，累有武功，廟號合稱祖。

translations.literal: The late emperor cut down rebels and bandits and repeatedly had military achievements; the temple name ought to be styled zu."
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor suppressed rebellion with repeated military success; his temple name should be zu, not zong."

sentences.zh: 陛下正當決在宸斷，無信齷齪書生也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should decide this at the imperial throne; do not trust pedantic bookish scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The decision belongs to Your Majesty alone; do not heed narrow pedants.

sentences.zh: 」遂詔下公卿與禮官議其可否。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict was sent down to the dukes and ministers and ritual officials to debate whether it was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the chief ministers and ritual officers to debate the proposal.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王彥威奏議：「大行廟號，不宜稱祖，宜稱宗。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Yanwei memorialized: "The late emperor's temple name should not be styled Zu; it should be styled Zong."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Yanwei argued that the late emperor's temple name should be Zong, not Zu.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 其月，禮部奏：「准貞觀故事，遷廟之主，藏於夾室西壁南北三間。

translations.literal: That month the Ministry of Rites memorialized: "According to the Zhenguan precedent, removed temple tablets are stored in the three north–south chambers on the west wall of the side chambers."
translations.idiomatic: That month the Ministry of Rites cited Zhenguan precedent: removed tablets go in three chambers on the west wall of the side rooms.

sentences.zh: 第一間代祖室，第二間高宗室，第三間中宗室。

translations.literal: The first chamber was the chamber of the dynastic founder; the second, the chamber of Emperor Gaozong; the third, the chamber of Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: The first room was for the dynastic founder, the second for Gaozong, the third for Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 伏以山陵日近，睿宗皇帝祧遷有期，夾室西壁三室外，無置室處。

translations.literal: We note that the imperial tomb day draws near and Emperor Ruizong's removal is due; beyond the three chambers on the west wall of the side chambers there is no place to set a chamber.
translations.idiomatic: With Ruizong's enshrinement imminent, no room remained on the west side-chamber wall beyond the three existing chambers.

sentences.zh: 准《江都集禮》：『古者遷廟之主，藏於太室北壁之中。

translations.literal: According to the Jiangdu Collected Rites: "In antiquity removed temple tablets were stored within the north wall of the Grand Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdu Collected Rites say ancient removed tablets were kept in the Grand Chamber's north wall.

sentences.zh: 』今請於夾室北壁，以西為上，置睿宗皇帝神主石室。

translations.literal: " Now we request on the north wall of the side chambers, taking west as superior, to place the stone chamber for Emperor Ruizong's spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to place Ruizong's tablet chamber on the north wall of the side rooms, west taking precedence.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: " The decree followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 正月，禮儀使奏：「謹按《周禮》：『天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。

translations.literal: In the first month the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized: "We respectfully examine the Zhou Rites: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu, and with the temple of the Grand Ancestor they are seven.'"
translations.idiomatic: First month: the ritual commissioner cited the Zhou Rites on the Son of Heaven's seven temples—three zhao, three mu, plus the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 』《荀卿子》曰：『有天下者祭七代，有一國者祭五代。

translations.literal: " Xunzi says: "He who possesses All-under-Heaven sacrifices to seven generations; he who possesses one state sacrifices to five generations."
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi says a ruler of the realm sacrifices to seven generations, a feudal lord to five.

sentences.zh: 』則知天子上祭七廟，典籍通規。

translations.literal: " Thus we know that the Son of Heaven ascends to sacrifice at seven temples—this is the universal rule in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: So seven ancestral temples for the Son of Heaven is the classical norm.

sentences.zh: 祖功宗德，不在其數。

translations.literal: Ancestral merit and dynastic virtue are not counted in that number.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ancestors and dynastic founders lie outside that count.

sentences.zh: 國朝九廟之制，法周之文。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's system of nine ancestral temples follows the Zhou pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's nine-shrine system follows the Zhou model.

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝，始為唐公，肇基天命，義同周之后稷。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing, who first became Duke of Tang and inaugurated the Mandate, is analogous to Hou Ji of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing, first Duke of Tang and founder of the Mandate, matches Zhou's Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝，創業經始，代隋為唐，義同周之文王。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong the Divine Yao, who founded the enterprise and replaced Sui with Tang, is analogous to King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong the Divine Yao, who founded the dynasty, matches King Wen.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝，神武應期，造有區夏，義同周之武王。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong the Cultured, martial and responsive to the age, who made the realm, is analogous to King Wu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong the Cultured, who pacified the realm, matches King Wu.

sentences.zh: 其下三昭三穆，謂之親廟，四時常饗，自如禮文。

translations.literal: Below them the three zhao and three mu are called the intimate temples; seasonal offerings follow the ritual text as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Below them the three zhao and three mu are the "intimate" shrines with regular seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 今以新主入廟，玄宗明皇帝在三昭三穆之外，是親盡之祖，雖有功德，禮合祧遷，禘祫之歲，則從合食。

translations.literal: Now with a new tablet entering the temple, Emperor Xuanzong the Brilliant lies outside the three zhao and three mu; he is an ancestor whose line of descent is exhausted. Though he has merit and virtue, ritual requires removal; in the years of di and cha he joins the combined feast.
translations.idiomatic: With a new tablet enshrined, Xuanzong stood outside the zhao-mu line—an exhausted line despite his merit—and would be removed, joining the combined di and cha feast.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: " The decree followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: ，禮儀使奏：「謹按天子七廟，祖功宗德，不在其中。

translations.literal: , the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized: "We respectfully examine the Son of Heaven's seven temples: ancestral merit and dynastic virtue are not among them."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner again noted that meritorious ancestors and dynastic founders are outside the seven-temple count.

sentences.zh: 國朝制度，太廟九室。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's institution: the Grand Temple has nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Under dynastic practice the Grand Temple has nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 伏以太祖景皇帝受封于唐，高祖、太宗，創業受命，有功之主，百代不遷。

translations.literal: We note that the Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing received enfeoffment in Tang; Gaozong and Taizong founded the enterprise and received the Mandate—meritorious rulers are not removed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Jing, Gaozong, and Taizong—founders with merit—are never removed.

sentences.zh: 今文宗元聖昭獻皇帝升祔有時，代宗睿文孝武皇帝是親盡之祖，禮合祧遷，每至禘祫，合食如常。

translations.literal: Now Emperor Wenzong the Sagely Illustrious is due to ascend; Emperor Daizong the Sagely Cultured and Martial is an exhausted-line ancestor whom ritual requires to remove; at each di and cha he joins the combined feast as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong was to be enshrined; Daizong, an exhausted-line ancestor, would be removed yet share the di and cha feast as before.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 六月，制曰：「」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict said: "" [text not preserved in source].
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: an edict was issued, but its wording is lost in the source.

sentences.zh: 五月，禮儀使奏：

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「」尚書左丞鄭涯等奏議曰：「夫禮經垂則，莫重于嚴配，必參損益之道，則合典禮之文。

translations.literal: An edict said: "" [text not preserved in source]. Vice Minister of the Left Zheng Ya and others memorialized, saying: "The ritual classics set norms; nothing is weightier than the solemn matching sacrifice. One must consult the way of increase and decrease, then it accords with canonical ritual text."
translations.idiomatic: An edict (text lost) ordered debate; Vice Minister Zheng Ya and others said ritual norms above all govern the great matching sacrifice and must follow the classics with due adjustment.

sentences.zh: 況有明徵，是資折衷。

translations.literal: Moreover there are clear proofs—this supports a balanced decision.
translations.idiomatic: Clear precedents supported a balanced ruling.

sentences.zh: 伏自敬宗、文宗、武宗三朝嗣位，皆以兄弟，考之前代，理有顯據。

translations.literal: We note that Emperors Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong succeeded in turn, all as brothers; examining earlier ages, reason gives plain evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong had succeeded as brothers—a pattern with clear precedent in earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 今謹詳禮院所奏，並上稽古文，旁摭史氏，協於通變，允謂得宜。

translations.literal: Now we respectfully examine in detail what the Ritual Institute memorialized, and above trace ancient texts and on the side gather historians; it harmonizes with timely change and may be called fitting.
translations.idiomatic: They reviewed the Ritual Institute's proposal against classics and history and found it a timely, fitting compromise.

sentences.zh: 臣等商議，請依禮官所議。

translations.literal: Your subjects deliberated and request following what the ritual officers proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked to follow the ritual officers' recommendation.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，制追尊憲宗、順宗諡號，事下有司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict posthumously elevated the honorific titles of Emperors Xianzong and Shunzong; the matter was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: edict raised Xianzong's and Shunzong's posthumous titles and referred implementation to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 太常博士李稠奏請別造憲宗、順宗神主，改題新諡。

translations.literal: Erudite Li Chou memorialized requesting separately to make new spirit tablets for Xianzong and Shunzong and change the inscriptions to the new honorifics.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Li Chou asked to carve new tablets for Xianzong and Shunzong bearing the new titles.

sentences.zh: 上疑其事，詔都省集議。

translations.literal: The emperor doubted the matter and ordered the Department of State Affairs to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted this and ordered a joint deliberation at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中楊發、都官員外郎劉彥模等奏：「考尋故事，無別造神主改題之例。

translations.literal: Right Bureau Director Yang Fa, Director of Punishments Liu Yanmo, and others memorialized: "Examining precedents, there is no example of separately making spirit tablets and changing inscriptions."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fa and Liu Yanmo found no precedent for new tablets and retitled inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 」事在《楊發傳》。

translations.literal: " The matter is in the Biography of Yang Fa.
translations.idiomatic: The full debate is recorded in Yang Fa's biography.

sentences.zh: 時宰臣奏：「改造改題，並無所據，酌情順理，題則為宜。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers memorialized: "Remaking and retitling both lack authority; weighing sentiment and reason, retitling is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers argued remaking lacked precedent but retitling the existing tablets was reasonable.

sentences.zh: 況今士族之家，通行此例，雖尊卑有異，而情理則同。

translations.literal: Moreover among gentry families today this practice is common; though noble and base differ, sentiment and reason are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry families commonly retitled tablets; rank differed, but the principle was the same.

sentences.zh: 望就神主改題，則為通允。

translations.literal: We hope to retitle on the existing spirit tablets—then it will be broadly acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to retitle the existing tablets, which would be broadly acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」依之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯長安，僖宗避狄於成都府。

translations.literal: Huang Chao attacked Chang'an; Emperor Xizong avoided the Di barbarians at Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, Xizong fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，有司請享太祖已下十一室，詔公卿議其儀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer the responsible offices requested offering to the eleven chambers from the Grand Ancestor down; an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to debate the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: officers sought to sacrifice at all eleven shrines from the Grand Ancestor down; the court ordered debate on the rites.

sentences.zh: 太常卿牛叢與儒者同議其事。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Sacrifices Niu Cong deliberated the matter together with Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Director Niu Cong and the ritual scholars debated the matter.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「王者巡狩，以遷廟主行。

translations.literal: Someone said: "When the king tours the regions, he takes the removed temple tablets on the journey."
translations.idiomatic: Some cited the rule that a touring king carried removed ancestral tablets.

sentences.zh: 如無遷廟之主，則祝奉幣帛皮珪告于祖禰，遂奉以出，載于齋車，每舍奠焉。

translations.literal: If there are no removed temple tablets, the invoker presents silks, fabrics, pelts, and jade scepters to announce to the ancestors, then bears them out, loads them on the fasting carriage, and offers at each lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Without removed tablets, invokers would announce to the ancestors with silks and jade, then carry the tablets in the fasting carriage, offering at each stop.

sentences.zh: 今非巡狩，是失守宗廟。

translations.literal: Now this is not a tour—it is the loss of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: This was not a royal tour but the loss of the capital temple.

sentences.zh: 夫失守宗廟，則當罷宗廟之事。

translations.literal: When the ancestral temple is lost, ancestral temple affairs should be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was lost, its rites should cease.

sentences.zh: 」叢疑之。

translations.literal: " Cong doubted this.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Cong was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 將作監王儉、太子賓客李匡乂、虞部員外郎袁皓建議同異。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Construction Wang Jian, Palace Mentor Li Kuangyi, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Yuan Hao proposed differing plans.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Li Kuangyi, and Yuan Hao offered conflicting proposals.

sentences.zh: 及左丞崔厚為太常卿，遂議立行廟。

translations.literal: When Left Vice Director Cui Hou became Director of Imperial Sacrifices, they then resolved to establish a traveling temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hou became director, they resolved to set up a traveling temple.

sentences.zh: 以玄宗幸蜀時道宮玄元殿之前，架幄幕為十一室。

translations.literal: At the time when Emperor Xuanzong visited Shu, before the Daoist palace Hall of the Mysterious Origin, they erected curtain frames as eleven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They had once framed eleven curtained chambers before the Hall of the Mysterious Origin when Xuanzong fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 又無神主，題神版位而行事。

translations.literal: Again there were no spirit tablets; they inscribed spirit boards and conducted the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Without tablets they used inscribed boards and performed the rites.

sentences.zh: 達禮者非之，以為止之可也。

translations.literal: Those versed in ritual criticized this, holding that stopping would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual experts criticized the practice and said it should simply stop.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃特造神主以祔行廟。

translations.literal: The next year they specially made spirit tablets to enshrine in the traveling temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they specially carved tablets for the traveling temple.

sentences.zh: 十二月二十五日，僖宗再幸寶雞。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Emperor Xizong again visited Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of the twelfth month Xizong again reached Baoji.

sentences.zh: 其太廟十一室並祧廟八室及孝明太皇太后等別廟三室等神主，緣室法物，宗正寺官屬奉之隨駕鄠縣，為賊所劫，神主、法物皆遺失。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets of the Grand Temple's eleven chambers, the eight chambers of the removed temple, and the three separate temples of the Filial and Bright Grand Empress Dowager and others, together with ritual objects for the chambers, were escorted by officials of the Court of the Imperial Clan following the imperial progress to Hao County; bandits robbed them and the spirit tablets and ritual objects were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven Grand Temple tablets, eight removed-shrine tablets, three empress-dowager shrine tablets, and ritual gear—escorted by the clan court to Hao County—were looted and lost.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，車駕自興元還京，以宮室未備，權駐鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the imperial carriage returned to the capital from Xingyuan; because the palaces were not ready, it temporarily lodged at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, second month: the court returned from Xingyuan but lodged at Fengxiang while palaces were rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 禮院奏：「皇帝還宮，先謁太廟。

translations.literal: The Ritual Institute memorialized: "When the emperor returns to the palace, he first visits the Grand Temple."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Institute said the emperor should visit the Grand Temple first on returning.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟焚毀，神主失墜，請准禮例修奉者。

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temple is burned and destroyed and the spirit tablets are lost; we request following ritual precedent to restore and maintain them."
translations.idiomatic: With the temple burned and tablets lost, they asked to restore worship by precedent.

sentences.zh: 」禮院獻議曰：「按《春秋》：『新宮災，三日哭。

translations.literal: " The Ritual Institute presented a deliberation, saying: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals: 'When the new palace suffered fire, there was weeping for three days.'"
translations.idiomatic: The institute cited the Spring and Autumn: when the new palace burned, three days of mourning were prescribed.

sentences.zh: 』《傳》曰：『新宮，宣公廟也。

translations.literal: " The Commentary says: 'The new palace was Duke Xuan's temple.'"
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains the "new palace" was Duke Xuan's temple.

sentences.zh: 三日哭，禮也。

translations.literal: Weeping for three days is ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Three days of weeping was proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 』按《國史》，正月二日，太廟四室摧毀，時神主皆存，迎奉於太極殿安置，玄宗素服避正殿。

translations.literal: " According to the National History, on the second day of the first month four chambers of the Grand Temple collapsed; at the time the spirit tablets all survived and were welcomed and placed in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; Emperor Xuanzong wore plain dress and avoided the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: National History records: four Grand Temple chambers collapsed in the first month; tablets were saved to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and Xuanzong mourned in plain dress.

sentences.zh: ，肅宗還京師，以宗廟為賊所焚，於光順門外設次，向廟哭。

translations.literal: , when Emperor Suzong returned to the capital, because the ancestral temple had been burned by rebels, he set up a station outside Guangshun Gate and wept toward the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong returned, the rebels had burned the temple; he wept toward it from a station outside Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 歷檢故事，不見百官奉慰之儀。

translations.literal: Searching precedents through, one does not see the rite of the hundred officials coming to offer condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Precedents show no rite of officials offering formal condolence.

sentences.zh: 然上既素服避殿，百官奉慰，亦合情禮。

translations.literal: Yet since the emperor already wore plain dress and avoided the hall, the hundred officials offering condolence also fits sentiment and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with the emperor in mourning dress, officials' condolence was still fitting.

sentences.zh: 竊循故事，比附參詳，恐須宗正寺具宗廟焚毀及神主失墜事由奏，皇帝素服避殿，受慰訖，輟朝三日，下詔委少府監擇日依禮新造列聖神主。

translations.literal: We privately follow precedents and compare and examine in detail; we fear the Court of the Imperial Clan must report fully the burning of the ancestral temple and the loss of spirit tablets; the emperor in plain dress avoids the hall, receives condolence, then suspends court for three days, and issues an edict commissioning the Director of the Palace Workshops to choose a day by ritual to newly make the spirit tablets of the successive sages.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed: the clan court should report the disaster; the emperor mourn, receive officials' condolences, halt court three days, and order new sage tablets made on an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 如此方似合宜。

translations.literal: Only thus does it seem fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus would the rites be proper.

sentences.zh: 伏緣采栗須十一月，漸恐遲晚。

translations.literal: We note that gathering chestnut wood requires the eleventh month; we gradually fear it will be late.
translations.idiomatic: Chestnut wood for tablets required the eleventh month—they feared delay.

sentences.zh: 」修奉使宰相鄭延昌具議，中書門下奏曰：「伏以前年冬再有震驚，俄然巡寺，主司宗祝，迫以蒼黃。

translations.literal: " The restoration commissioner, Chancellor Zheng Yanchang, fully deliberated; the Secretariat memorialized, saying: "We note that last winter there were again shocks; suddenly the court moved to monasteries; the masters of sacrifice were pressed in haste."
translations.idiomatic: Restoration commissioner Zheng Yanchang and the Secretariat recalled last winter's shocks and the hasty flight that scattered the ritual officers.

sentences.zh: 伏緣移蹕鳳翔，未敢陳奏。

translations.literal: We note that because the court moved to Fengxiang, we did not dare memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: They had not yet reported while lodged at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 今則將回鑾輅，皆舉典章，清廟再營，孝思咸備。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage is about to return; all should uphold the canon; the pure temple will be rebuilt and filial thought fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne was returning, canon would be restored, and filial rebuilding of the temple could proceed.

sentences.zh: 伏請降敕，命所司參詳典禮修奉。

translations.literal: We respectfully request an edict ordering the offices to examine the canon in detail and restore and maintain it."
translations.idiomatic: They asked for an edict ordering offices to restore the temple by canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「」又修奉太廟使宰相鄭延昌奏：「太廟大殿十一室、二十三間、十一架，功績至大，計料支費不少。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "" [text not preserved in source]. Again the restoration commissioner for the Grand Temple, Chancellor Zheng Yanchang, memorialized: "The Grand Temple main hall has eleven chambers, twenty-three bays, and eleven roof frames—the achievement is very great and estimated expenses are not few."
translations.idiomatic: An edict (text lost); Zheng Yanchang added that rebuilding the eleven-chamber hall—twenty-three bays—would be vast and costly.

sentences.zh: 兼宗廟制度有數，難為損益。

translations.literal: Moreover ancestral temple institutions have fixed numbers; it is hard to increase or decrease them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple dimensions were fixed and hard to alter.

sentences.zh: 今不審依元料修奉，為復更有商量？

translations.literal: Now we do not know whether to restore according to the original estimates or again have further deliberation?
translations.idiomatic: Should restoration follow original plans or be renegotiated?

sentences.zh: 請下禮官詳議。

translations.literal: We request sending it down to ritual officers for detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: They asked ritual officers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 」太常博士殷盈孫奏議言：「如依元料，難以速成，況幣藏方虛，須資變禮。

translations.literal: " Erudite Yin Yingsun memorialized, saying: "If we follow the original estimates, it will be hard to complete quickly; moreover the treasury of silks is empty—we must rely on altered ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yin Yingsun said original plans could not be finished in time and empty treasuries required ritual adaptation.

sentences.zh: 竊以，以新修太廟未成，其新造神主，權于長安殿安置，便行饗告之禮，如同宗廟之儀，以俟廟成，方為遷祔。

translations.literal: We privately hold that, because the newly repaired Grand Temple is not finished, the newly made spirit tablets should temporarily be placed in the Hall of Everlasting Peace, and the offering and announcement rites carried out as in the ancestral temple, to await the temple's completion before enshrining.
translations.idiomatic: Until the new temple was done, new tablets should lodge in the Hall of Everlasting Peace for offering rites, then move when the temple stood.

sentences.zh: 今京城除充大內及正衙外，別無殿宇。

translations.literal: Now in the capital apart from filling the inner palace and main audience halls, there are no other halls.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from palace and audience halls, the capital had no spare halls.

sentences.zh: 伏聞先有詔旨，欲以少府監大廳權充太廟。

translations.literal: We have heard there was already an edict intending to use the great hall of the Director of the Palace Workshops as a temporary Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had proposed the Palace Workshops' great hall as a temporary temple.

sentences.zh: 其廳五間，伏緣十一室於五間之中陳設隘狹，請更接續修建，成十一間，以備十一室薦饗之所。

translations.literal: That hall has five bays; we note that setting out eleven chambers within five bays is cramped and narrow; we request further connected construction to make eleven bays as places for the eleven chambers' offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Five bays could not hold eleven shrines; they asked to extend the hall to eleven bays.

sentences.zh: 其三太后廟，即於少府監取西南屋三間，以備三室告饗所。

translations.literal: The three empress-dowager temples should take three rooms in the southwest of the Director of the Palace Workshops as places for the three chambers' announcement offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Three southwest rooms in the same compound would serve the three empress-dowager shrines.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨從之。

translations.literal: " The edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: ，將行禘祭，有司請以三太后神主祔饗於太廟。

translations.literal: , when the di sacrifice was about to be performed, the responsible offices requested enshrining the three empress-dowager spirit tablets in joint offering at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Before the di rite, officers proposed bringing the three empress-dowager tablets into the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 三太后者，孝明太皇太后鄭氏，宣宗之母也；

translations.literal: The three empress dowagers: Grand Empress Dowager Xiaoming, née Zheng, mother of Emperor Xuanzong;
translations.idiomatic: The three were Grand Empress Dowager Xiaoming (Zheng), Xuanzong's mother;

sentences.zh: 恭僖皇太后王氏，敬宗之母也；

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Gongxi, née Wang, mother of Emperor Jingzong;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Gongxi (Wang), Jingzong's mother;

sentences.zh: 貞獻皇太后蕭氏，文宗之母也。

translations.literal: and Grand Empress Dowager Zhenxian, née Xiao, mother of Emperor Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: and Grand Empress Dowager Zhenxian (Xiao), Wenzong's mother.

sentences.zh: 三后之崩，皆作神主，有故不當入太廟。

translations.literal: When the three empresses died, spirit tablets were all made; for reasons they should not enter the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Each had a tablet at death but should not enter the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 當時禮官建議並置別廟，每年五享，及三年一祫，五年一禘，皆於本廟行事，無奉神主入太廟之文。

translations.literal: At the time ritual officers proposed establishing separate temples for all, with five offerings yearly and cha every three years and di every five years—all conducted at their own temples, with no text of bringing spirit tablets into the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers had placed them in separate temples with their own seasonal and cha/di rites, never bringing tablets into the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 至是亂離之後，舊章散失，禮院憑《曲臺禮》，欲以三太后祔享太廟。

translations.literal: At this time after the turmoil the old regulations were scattered and lost; the Ritual Institute relied on Wang Yanwei's Quetai Rites and wished to enshrine the three empress dowagers in joint offering at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion the Ritual Institute, citing the Quetai Rites, sought to joint-offer the three empress dowagers in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 博士殷盈孫獻議非之，曰：

translations.literal: Erudite Yin Yingsun presented a memorial objecting, saying: [the memorial text is not preserved in the source].
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yin Yingsun objected in a memorial (text lost in the source).

sentences.zh: 宰相孔緯曰：「博士之言是也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Kong Wei said: "The erudite's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Kong Wei said Yin Yingsun was right.

sentences.zh: 昨禮院所奏儀注，今已敕下，大祭日迫，不可遽改，且依行之。

translations.literal: Yesterday the Ritual Institute's submitted protocol has now been edicted down; the great sacrifice day presses—it cannot be suddenly changed; for the time being let it be carried out as submitted."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei conceded the institute's rite was already ordered and the sacrifice was imminent—execute it for now.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂以三太后祔祫太廟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the three empress dowagers were enshrined in cha at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The three empress dowagers were nonetheless enshrined in the Grand Temple cha rite.

sentences.zh: 達禮者譏其大謬，至今未正。

translations.literal: Those versed in ritual mocked the great error; it has not been corrected to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual experts condemned the blunder, still uncorrected.

sentences.zh: 十一月，太常博士任疇上言：「去月十七日，饗德明、興聖廟，得廟直候論狀，稱懿祖室在獻祖室之上，當時雖以為然，便依行事，猶牒報監察使及宗正寺，請過示詳窺玉牒，如有不同，即相知聞奏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Erudite Ren Chou submitted, saying: "On the seventeenth of last month, offering at the Deming and Xingsheng temples, we received a report from the temple attendant Hou Lun's petition, stating that the chamber of Emperor Yi was above the chamber of Emperor Xian; though it was then deemed correct and the rite was performed, we still dispatched notice to the surveillance commissioner and the Court of the Imperial Clan, requesting examination of the imperial genealogy; if there is any difference, inform each other and memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: Erudite Ren Chou reported that at last month's offering at Deming and Xingsheng temples, attendants said Yi's shrine stood above Xian's—done provisionally but referred to genealogy for verification.

sentences.zh: 爾後伏檢《高祖神堯皇帝本紀》，伏審獻祖為懿祖之昭，懿祖為獻祖之穆，昭穆之位，天地極殊。

translations.literal: Thereafter your subject examined the Basic Annals of the Divine Yao Emperor Gaozu and found that the Ancestor of Offerings was the zhao of the Ancestor of Eminence, and the Ancestor of Eminence was the mu of the Ancestor of Offerings—the positions of zhao and mu are as far apart as Heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject found that the Ancestor of Offerings was zhao to the Ancestor of Eminence and the Ancestor of Eminence was mu to the Ancestor of Offerings—zhao and mu stand as far apart as heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 今廟室奪倫，不即陳奏，然尚為苟且，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Now the temple chambers usurp proper order, yet it was not reported at once; still to temporize is an offense that brooks no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine order is violated yet was not reported; to temporize is unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 仍敕修撰朱儔、檢討王皞研精詳復，得報稱：『，制追尊咎繇為德明皇帝，涼武昭王為興聖皇帝。

translations.literal: An edict still ordered Compiler Zhu Chou and Reviewer Wang Hao to examine with care; the reply stated: "In the second year of Zhide, an edict posthumously honored Gao Yao as Emperor Deming and the Martial Illustrious King of Liang as Emperor Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chou and Wang Hao were ordered to review; the reply cited Zhide 2: Gao Yao was made Emperor Deming and the Liang Martial Illustrious King Emperor Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 十載，立廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, temples were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year temples were set up.

sentences.zh: 至，制從給事中陳京、右僕射姚南仲等一百五十人之議，以為禘、袷是祖宗以序之祭，凡有國者必尊太祖。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, an edict followed the deliberation of 150 men led by Supervising Secretary Chen Jing and Right Vice Director Yao Nanzong, holding that di and xia are sequential sacrifices to the ancestors and that every state must honor its Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe the court followed Chen Jing, Yao Nanzong, and 150 others: di and xia are ordered ancestral rites; every state honors its Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 今國家以景皇帝為太祖，太祖之上，施於禘、袷，不可為位。

translations.literal: Now the state takes Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor; above the Grand Ancestor, to extend di and xia, no position can be set.
translations.idiomatic: The state takes Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor; above him no place may be made in di and xia.

sentences.zh: 請按德明、興聖廟共成四室，祔遷獻、懿二祖。

translations.literal: We ask that according to the Deming and Xingsheng temples together forming four chambers, the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence be enshrined and moved.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Deming and Xingsheng shrines form four chambers and receive the relocated Offerings and Eminence ancestors.

sentences.zh: 』謹尋儔等所報，即當時表奏，並獻居懿上。

translations.literal: " Your subject respectfully traced what Chou and others reported—that was the memorial of the time—and all placed Offerings above Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Chou’s report was the original memorial: Offerings was always above Eminence.

sentences.zh: 伏以國之大事，宗廟為先，禘、祫之禮，不當失序。

translations.literal: Your subject notes that the great affairs of the state put the ancestral temple first; the rites of di and xia must not lose order.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs begin with the ancestral temple; di and xia must keep their order.

sentences.zh: 四十餘載，理難尋詰。

translations.literal: More than forty years have passed; it is hard to pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years have passed—too late to trace easily.

sentences.zh: 伏祈聖鑒，即垂詔敕，具禮遷正。

translations.literal: Your subject prays the sacred discernment may at once issue an edict and complete the rites of relocation and correction.
translations.idiomatic: We beg an edict to correct the rites at once.

sentences.zh: 」其月，疇又奏曰：「伏聞今月十三日敕，以臣所奏獻、懿祖二室倒置事，宜令禮官集議聞奏者。

translations.literal: " That month, Zhou again memorialized: "Your subject has heard that on the thirteenth of this month an edict, on your subject’s report of the inverted placement of the two chambers of the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence, ordered the ritual officers to assemble for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhou again wrote: on the thirteenth an edict ordered ritual officers to debate his report that Offerings and Eminence were reversed.

sentences.zh: 臣去月十七日，緣遇太廟祫饗太祖景皇帝已下群主，准所祔獻、懿祖於德明廟，共為四室。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth of last month, because of the xia offering in the Grand Temple to the spirit tablets from Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing downward, according to the enshrinement of the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence in the Deming temple, together as four chambers.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth last month, at the Grand Temple xia for tablets from Emperor Jing down, Offerings and Eminence were placed in the Deming shrine as four chambers.

sentences.zh: 准元敕，各於本室行享禮。

translations.literal: According to the original edict, each was to receive offerings in its own chamber.
translations.idiomatic: By the original edict each tablet was served in its own chamber.

sentences.zh: 審知獻祖合居懿祖之上，昭穆方正。

translations.literal: It was clear that the Ancestor of Offerings should stand above the Ancestor of Eminence and that zhao and mu were correct.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings should stand above Eminence—zhao and mu in proper order.

sentences.zh: 其時親見獻祖之室，倒居懿祖之下。

translations.literal: At the time your subject personally saw the chamber of the Ancestor of Offerings placed inverted below that of the Ancestor of Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: He saw Offerings’ chamber placed below Eminence’s.

sentences.zh: 於後遍校圖籍，實見差殊，遂敢聞奏。

translations.literal: Afterward, comparing registers throughout, the discrepancy was real; your subject therefore dared to report.
translations.idiomatic: Registers later confirmed the error; he reported it.

sentences.zh: 今奉敕宜令禮官集議聞奏者。

translations.literal: Now, receiving the edict that ritual officers should assemble for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: Now the edict required ritual officers to debate and report.

sentences.zh: 臣得奉禮郎李岡、太祝柳仲年、協律郎諸葛畋李潼、檢討官王皞、修撰朱儔、博士閔慶之等七人伏稱：『謹按《高祖神堯皇帝本紀》及皇室圖譜，並武德、貞觀、永徽、開元已來諸禮著在甲令者，並云獻祖宣皇帝是神堯之高祖，懿祖光皇帝是神堯皇帝之曾祖，以高曾辨之，則獻祖是懿祖之父，懿祖是獻祖之子。

translations.literal: Your subject obtained seven men—Director of Offerings Li Gang, Grand Invocator Liu Zhongnian, Harmonizing Officer Zhuge Tian, Li Tong, Reviewer Wang Hao, Compiler Zhu Chou, and Erudite Min Qingzhi—who stated: "Respectfully according to the Basic Annals of the Divine Yao Emperor Gaozu and the imperial genealogy, and all ritual codes recorded in statutes from Wude, Zhenguan, Yonghui, and Kaiyuan onward, all say that the Ancestor of Offerings Emperor Xuan was Gaozu’s great-grandfather and the Ancestor of Eminence Emperor Guang was Gaozu’s great-great-grandfather; by great-grandfather and great-great-grandfather, the Ancestor of Offerings was father to the Ancestor of Eminence and the Ancestor of Eminence was son to the Ancestor of Offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Seven officers—Li Gang, Liu Zhongnian, Zhuge Tian, Li Tong, Wang Hao, Zhu Chou, Min Qingzhi—cited annals and genealogy: Offerings Xuan was Gaozu’s great-grandfather, Eminence Guang his great-great-grandfather; Offerings was Eminence’s father.

sentences.zh: 即博士任疇所奏倒祀不虛。

translations.literal: Thus Erudite Ren Zhou’s report of inverted sacrifice is not false.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhou’s charge of inverted worship was true.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏乞即垂詔敕，具禮遷正。

translations.literal: Your subject prays that an edict be issued at once to complete the rites of relocation and correction."
translations.idiomatic: They asked for an edict to correct the placement.

translations.literal: The memorial concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial closed.

sentences.zh: 其事遂行。

translations.literal: The matter was then carried out.
translations.idiomatic: It was done.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自興元還京，夏四月，將行禘祭，有司引舊儀：「禘德明、興聖二廟，及懿祖、獻祖神主祔興聖、德明廟，通為四室。

translations.literal: When Xizong returned to the capital from Xingyuan, in the fourth month of summer they were to perform the di sacrifice; the responsible offices cited the old protocol: "Di at the Deming and Xingsheng temples, and the spirit tablets of the Ancestors of Eminence and Offerings enshrined in the Xingsheng and Deming temples, four chambers in all."
translations.idiomatic: Xizong returned from Xingyuan; in summer’s fourth month, before the di rite, offices cited old practice: di at Deming and Xingsheng, with Offerings and Eminence in four chambers.

sentences.zh: 」黃巢之亂，廟已焚毀，及是將禘，俾議其儀。

translations.literal: In the chaos of Huang Chao, the temples had been burned; when the di was now to be held, they were ordered to deliberate the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had burned the temples; rites for the coming di had to be reworked.

sentences.zh: 博士殷盈孫議曰：「臣以德明等四廟，功非創業，義止追封，且於今皇帝年代極遙，昭穆甚遠。

translations.literal: Erudite Yin Yingsun argued: "Your subject holds that the four temples of Deming and the rest achieved no founding merit and were posthumous ennoblements only; moreover they are extremely remote in date from the present emperor and very distant in zhao-mu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yingsun argued the four shrines lacked founding merit, were only posthumous honors, and were too remote in descent.

sentences.zh: 可依晉韋泓『屋毀乃已』之例，因而廢之。

translations.literal: One may follow the Jin precedent of Wei Hong, "when the house is destroyed, stop," and abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Wei Hong’s Jin rule: when the building is gone, cease—and abolish them.

sentences.zh: 」敕下百僚都省會議，禮部員外薛昭緯奏議曰：

translations.literal: " An edict was sent down for joint deliberation in the Department of State Affairs; Vice Director of Rites Xue Zhaowei submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: The edict went to the Department of State Affairs; Xue Zhaowei of Rites memorialized:

sentences.zh: 奉敕敬依典禮，付所司。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict, we respectfully follow the canonical rites and refer the matter to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed the canon and referred execution to the offices.

sentences.zh: 正月，制以籩、豆之薦，或未能備物，宜令禮官學士詳議具奏。

translations.literal: In the first month, an edict held that in the offering of baskets and beans, vessels might not be complete; ritual officers and academicians were to deliberate in detail and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: First month: an edict said basket-and-bean offerings might be incomplete and ordered ritual scholars to report.

sentences.zh: 太常卿韋縚請「宗廟之奠，每室籩、豆各加十二。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Zou requested: "For offerings in the ancestral temple, let each chamber have twelve baskets and twelve beans added.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zou asked twelve more baskets and twelve more beans per ancestral chamber.

sentences.zh: 又今之酌獻酒爵，制度全小，僅無一合，執持甚難，請稍令廣大。

translations.literal: Moreover the present wine cups for libation are wholly small, barely one he in measure, and very hard to hold; we ask that they be made somewhat larger.
translations.idiomatic: Libation cups were tiny—barely one he—and hard to hold; he asked they be enlarged.

sentences.zh: 其郊祀奠獻，亦准此。

translations.literal: Suburban and border offerings should follow this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban offerings should follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 仍望付尚書省集眾官詳議，務從折衷。

translations.literal: We also hope the Department of State Affairs may gather all officials for detailed deliberation and seek a balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the Department of State Affairs to gather officials and find a middle course.

sentences.zh: 」於是兵部侍郎張均及職方郎中韋述等建議曰：

translations.literal: " Thereupon Vice Director of War Zhang Jun and Bureau Director Wei Shu and others submitted recommendations:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun and Wei Shu then offered recommendations:

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎楊仲昌議曰：「謹按《禮》曰：『夫祭不欲煩，煩則黷；

translations.literal: Vice Director of Rites Yang Zhongchang argued: "Respectfully according to the Rites: 'Sacrifice should not be troublesome—if troublesome it becomes irreverent;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongchang cited the Rites: sacrifice must not be burdensome or it becomes irreverent;

sentences.zh: 亦不欲簡，簡則怠。

translations.literal: nor should it be too simple—if too simple it becomes negligent.'
translations.idiomatic: nor too simple, or it becomes negligent.

sentences.zh: 』又鄭玄云：『人生尚褻食，鬼神則不然。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also said: 'While the living esteem coarse food, spirits are not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said the living eat coarsely but spirits do not.

sentences.zh: 神農時雖有黍稷，猶未有酒醴。

translations.literal: In the time of Shennong there were millet and panic grass but still no wine or ale.
translations.idiomatic: In Shennong’s age there was grain but no wine.

sentences.zh: 及後聖作為醴酪，猶存玄酒，求不忘古。

translations.literal: When later sages made ale and cheese, they still kept the dark liquor, seeking not to forget antiquity.'
translations.idiomatic: Later sages made ale yet kept dark liquor to remember antiquity.

sentences.zh: 』《春秋》曰：『蘋蘩、蘊藻之菜，潢汙行潦之水，可羞于王公，可薦於鬼神。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals says: 'Water-cress and pondweed, water from puddles and roadside ditches, may be set before kings and dukes and offered to spirits.'
translations.idiomatic: The Annals say pondweed and ditch water may honor kings and spirits.

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『大羹不和，粢食不鑿。

translations.literal: It also says: 'Great broth unseasoned, millet food unpolished.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says great broth is unseasoned and millet left unpolished.

sentences.zh: 』此明君人者，有國奉先，敬神嚴享，豈肥濃以為尚，將儉約以表誠。

translations.literal: This shows that rulers with a state who serve their ancestors and revere spirits in solemn offering do not take richness and heaviness as the standard but use frugality to show sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers honor ancestors by frugality, not by rich food.

sentences.zh: 則陸海之物，鮮肥之類，既乖禮文之情，而變作者之法，皆充祭用，非所詳也。

translations.literal: Then goods from land and sea and fresh, fatty kinds, being contrary to ritual sentiment and to the law of offerings, if all were used in sacrifice, are not to be approved.
translations.idiomatic: Sea and land delicacies violate ritual and should not all enter sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『樽酒簋貳，用缶，納約自牖。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'One wine vessel, two gui of grain, using an earthenware jar, presenting the offering through the window.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes prescribe one wine vessel and two gui in an earthen jar.

sentences.zh: 』此明祭存簡易，不在繁奢。

translations.literal: This shows sacrifice keeps to simplicity and lies not in multiplicity and luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice should be simple, not lavish.

sentences.zh: 所以一樽之酒，貳簋之奠，為明祀也。

translations.literal: Therefore one vessel of wine and two gui of offering make the meaning of sacrifice clear.
translations.idiomatic: One wine and two gui suffice for clear sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，夫義以出禮，禮以體政，違則有紊，是稱不經。

translations.literal: Moreover it is heard that righteousness produces ritual and ritual embodies government; to violate it is disorder—this is called uncanonical.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness begets ritual; ritual embodies government—violation is disorder.

sentences.zh: 薦肥濃則褻味有登，加籩爵則事非師古。

translations.literal: To offer rich and heavy flavors is to set coarse tastes on high; to add baskets and cups is to depart from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Rich offerings vulgarize taste; added baskets and cups abandon antiquity.

sentences.zh: 與其別行新制，寧如謹守舊章？

translations.literal: Rather than institute a new rule separately, is it not better to guard the old statutes carefully?"
translations.idiomatic: Better keep the old statutes than invent new ones.

sentences.zh: 」時太子賓客崔沔、戶部郎中楊伯成、左衛兵曹劉秩等皆建議以為請依舊禮，不可改易。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Guest Cui Mian, Bureau Director Yang Bocheng, Left Guard Army Cao Liu Zhi, and others all argued to follow the old rites and not change them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian, Yang Bocheng, Liu Zhi, and others all urged keeping the old rites.

sentences.zh: 於是宰臣等具沔、述等議以奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers presented the recommendations of Mian, Shu, and the rest for memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers submitted Mian’s and Shu’s views.

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「」以是更令太常量加品味。

translations.literal: Xuanzong said: "We inherit our ancestors' accumulated virtue; as to offerings of grain in sacrifice, We truly wish them full and rich; the vessels for ritual should show loyal intent. What is not fragrant and pure or not in accord with regulation may not be used." Thereupon he again ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to add flavors regularly.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong said he wished offerings rich yet excluded what was impure or uncanonical, then ordered the Court of Sacrifices to add flavors.

sentences.zh: 韋縚又奏：「請每室加籩、豆各六，每四時異品，以當時新果及珍羞同薦。

translations.literal: Wei Zou again memorialized: "We ask that six baskets and six beans be added to each chamber, and each season's different products, with seasonal fruit and delicacies offered together."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zou asked six more baskets and beans per chamber plus seasonal fruit.

sentences.zh: 」則可之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 又酌獻酒爵，玄宗令用龠升一升，合于古義，而多少適中。

translations.literal: As to the libation cups, Xuanzong ordered the use of the yue sheng of one sheng, in accord with ancient meaning and moderate in amount.
translations.idiomatic: Libation cups were set at one sheng by the yue measure—ancient and moderate.

sentences.zh: 自是常依行焉。

translations.literal: From then on this was regularly followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this practice stood.

sentences.zh: 後漢世祖光武皇帝葬于原陵，其子孝明帝追思不已。

translations.literal: Later Han Emperor Guangwu was buried at Yuanling; his son Emperor Ming never ceased to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu of Later Han was buried at Yuanling; his son Ming long mourned him.

sentences.zh: ，乃率諸侯王、公卿，正月朝于原陵，親奉先后陰氏妝奩篋笥悲慟，左右侍臣，莫不嗚咽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongyuan he led the feudal princes, kings, and ministers in the first month to attend Yuanling, personally presenting the dressing cases and toilet boxes of the late Empress Yin with grief; the attendants at his side all wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan 2: Ming led princes and ministers to Yuanling in the first month, weeping over Yin’s toilet goods while attendants sobbed.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝父丹陽尹順之，追尊為太祖文帝，先葬丹徒，亦尊為建陵。

translations.literal: Liang Wudi’s father, Director of Danyang Shunzhi, was posthumously honored as Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen and was first buried at Dantu; he was also honored as Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi’s father Shunzhi, made Grand Ancestor Wen, lay at Dantu and Jianling.

sentences.zh: 武帝即大位後，，亦朝於建陵，有紫雲廕覆陵上，食頃方滅。

translations.literal: After Wudi took the throne, he also attended Jianling; purple clouds shaded the mound and only after a meal’s time did they disperse.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession Wudi visited Jianling; purple clouds covered the mound briefly.

sentences.zh: 梁主著單衣介幘，設次而拜，望陵流哭，淚之所沾，草皆變色。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler wore a single garment and a kerchief, set up a tent and bowed, gazed at the mound and wept streaming tears; where the tears fell, the grass changed color.
translations.idiomatic: He wore plain dress, bowed at a tent, wept until the grass changed color where tears fell.

sentences.zh: 陵傍有枯泉，至時而水流香潔。

translations.literal: Beside the mound was a dry spring that at the time flowed fragrant and clear.
translations.idiomatic: A dry spring beside the tomb briefly flowed sweet and clear.

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「陵陰石虎，與陵俱創二百餘年，恨小，可更造碑石柱麟，並二陵中道門為三闥。

translations.literal: He therefore told his attendants: "The stone tigers by the mound were made with the mound more than two hundred years ago; regretting their small size, they may be remade as steles, stone pillars, and qilin, and the middle gate of the two mounds made into three gates.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered larger steles, pillars, and qilin and three gates for the spirit path—the old stone tigers were too small.

sentences.zh: 園陵職司，並賜一級。

translations.literal: The staff of the park and tombs were all promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mausoleum staff were promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 」奉辭諸陵，哭踴而拜。

translations.literal: " Having paid respects at the various mounds, he wept and bowed in the full mourning leap.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave of each tomb with weeping and the mourning leap.

sentences.zh: 周太祖文帝葬于成陵，其子明帝初立，元年十二月，謁於成陵。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Grand Ancestor Wen was buried at Chengling; his son Emperor Ming, on first accession, in the twelfth month of the first year, visited Chengling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Grand Ancestor Wen lay at Chengling; Ming visited in the twelfth month of his first year.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯葬於獻陵，正月乙巳，太宗朝於獻陵。

translations.literal: Gaozu Shenyao was buried at Xianling; on the day yisi of the first month, Taizong attended Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu lay at Xianling; Taizong visited on the first month’s yisi day.

sentences.zh: 先是日，宿衛設黃麾仗周衛陵寢，至是質明，七廟子孫及諸侯百僚、蕃夷君長皆陪列于司馬門內。

translations.literal: On the day before, the guard set yellow awnings and surrounded the tomb precinct; at daybreak the descendants of the seven temples, the feudal lords, the hundred officials, and tribal chieftains all stood in ranks inside the Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, guards ringed the tomb; at dawn imperial kin, nobles, officials, and chieftains lined the Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至小次，降輿納履，哭于闕門，西面再拜，慟絕不能興。

translations.literal: The emperor reached the small shelter, descended the carriage, put on shoes, wept at the gate tower facing west and bowed twice, and was overcome and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept twice west of the gate tower and could not rise.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，改服入于寢宮，親執饌，閱視高祖及先后服御之物，匍匐床前悲慟。

translations.literal: When the rites were done, he changed dress and entered the sleeping palace, personally held the food trays, and inspected the garments and goods of Gaozu and the late empress, crawling before the bed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the sleeping palace, inspected Gaozu’s and the empress’s goods, and wept before the bed.

sentences.zh: 左右侍御者莫不歔欷。

translations.literal: Those attending at left and right all sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants all wept.

sentences.zh: 初，甲辰之夜，大雨雪。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the night of jiachen, great rain and snow had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The night before jiachen brought heavy snow.

sentences.zh: 及皇帝入陵院，悲號哽咽，百辟哀慟，是時雪益甚，寒風暴起，有蒼雲出於山陵之上，俄而流布，天地晦冥。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the tomb precinct, wailing and sobbing, the hundred ministers grieved; at that time the snow increased, a cold wind rose violently, and dark clouds issued from above the hill-tomb, soon spreading; heaven and earth were dim.
translations.idiomatic: As he entered the precinct all wailed; snow thickened, wind rose, dark clouds spread from the mound.

sentences.zh: 至禮畢，皇帝出自寢宮，步過司馬門北，泥行二百餘步，於是風靜雪止，雲氣歇滅，天色開霽。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished and the emperor came out from the sleeping palace, he walked north past the Sima Gate, treading mud for more than two hundred paces; then the wind stilled, the snow stopped, the clouds dispersed, and the sky cleared.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he walked two hundred paces in mud north of the Sima Gate; then wind and snow ceased and the sky cleared.

sentences.zh: 觀者竊議，以為孝感之所致焉。

translations.literal: Onlookers privately said it was brought about by filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers called it filial piety moving heaven.

sentences.zh: 是日曲赦三原縣及從官衛士等，大辟已下，已發覺，未發覺，皆釋其罪。

translations.literal: That day a partial amnesty was granted to Sanyuan County and the attendant guards and officers; for capital crimes and below, whether discovered or not, all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: That day Sanyuan and the guard received partial amnesty through capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 免民一年租賦。

translations.literal: The people’s one-year land tax and corvée were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: A year’s land tax was remitted.

sentences.zh: 有八十已上，及孝子順孫、義夫節婦、鰥寡孤獨、有篤疾者，賜物各有差。

translations.literal: Those eighty and above, filial sons and compliant grandsons, righteous husbands and chaste wives, widowers, orphans, and solitaries, and those with grave illness received gifts in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The aged, the filial, the chaste, widows, orphans, and the gravely ill received graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 宿衛陵邑中郎將、衛士齋員及三原令以下，各賜爵一級。

translations.literal: The Central Guard lieutenant of the tomb district, fast-day guards, and all from the magistrate of Sanyuan downward each received promotion of one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb guards and officials through the magistrate of Sanyuan gained one rank.

sentences.zh: 丁未，至自獻陵。

translations.literal: On dingwei, he returned from Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he returned from Xianling.

sentences.zh: 己酉，朝於太極殿。

translations.literal: On jiyou, he attended court at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou he held court at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 庚子，會群臣，奏《功成慶善》及《破陣》之樂。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he gathered the ministers and presented the music "Achievement Complete, Celebration of Good" and "Breaking the Battle Line."
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he had ministers hear Achievement Complete and Breaking the Battle Line.

sentences.zh: 玄宗十一月丙申，親謁橋陵。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen of the eleventh month, Xuanzong personally visited Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month bingchen: Xuanzong visited Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 皇帝望陵涕泣，左右並哀感。

translations.literal: Gazing at the mound, the emperor wept; those at his left and right were all moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: He wept at the mound; attendants grieved with him.

sentences.zh: 進奉先縣同赤縣，以所管萬三百戶供陵寢，三府兵馬供衛，曲赦縣內大辟罪已下。

translations.literal: Fengxian County was advanced to the status of a red county; its 103,000 households were assigned to supply the tomb, and troops of the three metropolitan prefectures to guard; a partial amnesty within the county for crimes below capital grade.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian became a red county; 103,000 households supplied the tomb; three prefectures guarded; the county was partially amnestied.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，謁定陵。

translations.literal: On wuxu, he visited Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he visited Dingling.

sentences.zh: 己亥，謁獻陵。

translations.literal: On jihai, he visited Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he visited Xianling.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，謁昭陵。

translations.literal: On renyin, he visited Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he visited Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 己巳，謁乾陵。

translations.literal: On jisi, he visited Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he visited Qianling.

sentences.zh: 戊申，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On wushen, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，流移人並放還，左降官移近處，百姓無出今年地稅之半。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm; displaced persons were all sent home; demoted officials were moved nearer; the people paid no more than half this year’s land tax.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied the realm, sent exiles home, moved demoted officials nearer, and halved the land tax.

sentences.zh: 每陵取側近六鄉以供陵寢。

translations.literal: For each tomb, six neighboring townships were taken to supply the tomb precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Six townships near each tomb supplied the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初至橋陵，質明，柏樹甘露降，曙後祥煙遍空。

translations.literal: When the emperor first reached Qiaoling, at daybreak sweet dew fell on the cypress trees; after dawn auspicious mist filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: At Qiaoling dawn brought dew on cypresses and auspicious mist after sunrise.

sentences.zh: 皇帝謁昭陵，陪葬功臣盡來受饗，鳳吹釭釭，若神祇之所集。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Zhaoling, the meritorious ministers buried with him all came to receive offerings; phoenix music rang clearly as if spirits were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhaoling companion ministers received offerings; phoenix music rang as if spirits gathered.

sentences.zh: 陪位文武百僚皆聞先聖歎息、功臣蹈舞之聲，皆以為至孝所感。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials in attendance all heard the sighs of the former sage and the treading dance of the meritorious ministers, and all took it as a response to utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Attending officials heard sighs and dancing—they called it utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 八月，制：「」十三載，改獻、昭、乾、定、橋五陵署為臺，其署令改為臺令，加舊一級。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict: "Henceforth, on the first day of the ninth month each year, garments shall be offered at the tomb palaces." In the thirteenth year, the five mausoleum offices of Xian, Zhao, Qian, Ding, and Qiao were changed to directorates; their directors became directorate chiefs, one rank above the former grade.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: edicts for annual ninth-month garment offerings at the tombs; in year 13 five mausoleum offices became directorates with higher-ranked chiefs.
